components.name: AccessibilityProvider
components.description: AccessibilityProvider applies the reader settings to the page and stores them on the device; useAccessibility reads them, for example to skip an animation. AccessibilitySettings is the ready settings section, and takes extra rows such as a ThemeToggle.

examples.code:
<AccessibilityProvider>
  <AccessibilitySettings labels={labels}>
    <ThemeToggle label="Theme" options={options} />
  </AccessibilitySettings>
</AccessibilityProvider>

const { motionReduced } = useAccessibility()

components.a11y: Text size is a spin button: arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End step it, and the minus and plus buttons give pointer users 44px targets. Each setting is a switch named by its title and described by its hint. A system request for reduced motion always wins and locks that switch on. Restore defaults is confirmed through a polite live region.

components.name: ActivityBar
components.description: The column of view icons on the start edge of the desktop app. ActivityItem shows a view with a tip, a shortcut and a badge; pin settings and help to the bottom with footer.

examples.code:
<ActivityBar label="Views" footer={<ActivityItem label="Settings" onPress={…}><Icon name="nav.settings" /></ActivityItem>}>
  <ActivityItem label="Agents" tip="Terminals and chats" shortcut="⌘2" badge={2} badgeLabel="2 waiting" isCurrent><Icon name="agent.bot" /></ActivityItem>
</ActivityBar>

components.a11y: A navigation landmark with a list of 40px buttons named by their labels. The current view has aria-current="page", the accent and a rule on the edge. badgeLabel is read with the name and shown in the tip, so the count never relies on its colour. Tips open on hover and keyboard focus, close on Escape and stay while hovered.

components.name: ActivityHeatmap
components.description: Daily activity over months as a calendar, one column per week, such as commits over a year. Pick it to show rhythm and streaks; pick a bar chart for exact daily counts over a few weeks.

examples.code:
<ActivityHeatmap
  label="Contributions, last 12 months"
  days={days}
  formatValue={(count) => t('commits', { count })}
  keyboardHint="Arrow keys move by day and by week."
  lessLabel="Less"
  moreLabel="More"
  table={{ trigger: 'Show days with activity', dateHeader: 'Date', valueHeader: 'Commits' }}
/>

components.a11y: One tab stop over the whole calendar. Up and Down move a day, Left and Right a week, Home and End to the ends; each day is read with its full date, its count and its sources through a polite live region, and Escape hides the tooltip. The box scrolls on its own on a narrow screen, opens at the latest week and follows the focus. Shades are steps of one colour, and the count is always in words in the tooltip, the reading and the table. Cells keep an outline and use system colours in forced colours.

components.name: AgentAvatar
components.description: The square letter tile of a coding agent, in session lists, tabs and chips. The app passes the letters and the colour from its agent list.

examples.code: <AgentAvatar letters="C" color="var(--sk-tool-agent)" label="Claude Code" />

components.a11y: Decoration unless label is set. The letters stay on the foreground token over a tint of at most 24 percent, which keeps text contrast above 4.5:1 for any colour, and the full colour goes to the border.

components.name: AgentBoard
components.description: Several sessions side by side, one to three columns by the board’s own width. Pick it for the main area of an agents view; it has room for an empty state, a loading state and a message on top.

examples.code:
<AgentBoard label={t('board', { workspace })} emptyState={<EmptyState … />} notice={offline ? <Alert … /> : null}>
  {sessions.map((s) => <AgentPane key={s.id} … />)}
</AgentBoard>

components.a11y: The board is a named region and reads its panes in order. Below 42rem of width the panes stack in one column with a minimum height, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px or at 400% zoom. Loading is a polite progress bar with its own name and sets aria-busy. Put messages in notice as an Alert: a warning or an error keeps its icon and word, and the notice sits in a polite live region from the first render, so it is read out when it appears.

components.name: AgentChip
components.description: An agent as a small pill with its avatar, name and version, for the row of ready agents. A missing agent gets a dashed edge and can become the button that installs it.

examples.code:
<AgentChip name="Codex" letters="X" detail="0.9" />
<AgentChip
  name="Aider" letters="A" available={false}
  unavailableLabel="not installed" actionLabel="Install"
  onPress={install} isPending={installing}
/>

components.a11y: A missing agent is shown by a dashed edge and a download glyph, and unavailableLabel is read, so fading is never the only sign. As a button its name is the agent, the state and actionLabel. While pending it keeps focus, ignores presses and React Aria announces it as busy. Long names truncate inside the chip, which never grows past its container.

components.name: AgentOverview
components.description: Every session at a glance as cards with the last lines of each screen, most urgent first. Pick it for a quick switcher across many sessions, often in a dialog behind a shortcut.

examples.code:
<AgentOverview label={t('allSessions')} order={ids} onOpen={open}>
  {sessions.map((s, i) => (
    <AgentOverviewCard key={s.id} id={s.id} title={s.title} state={s.state} stateLabel={…} lines={s.screen} shortcut={String(i + 1)} />
  ))}
</AgentOverview>

components.a11y: A React Aria grid list: arrow keys move in two dimensions, Enter opens the focused card and the digits 1 to 9 open the matching card. Each card reads its title, state and folder; the screen picture is hidden from screen readers, who open the session to read it. Blocked and done cards get a thick leading edge as well as their word. Columns follow the width, down to one at 320px.

components.name: AgentPane
components.description: One session on a board: a header, the terminal or chat, and a toolbar. Pick it for each agent or shell the user runs; the frame shows when the session waits for them or is picked for a broadcast.

examples.code:
<AgentPane
  state={session.state}
  isSelected={picked}
  header={<AgentPaneHeader title={session.title} state={<SessionStateChip … />} />}
  footer={<TerminalBar label={t('tools')}>…</TerminalBar>}
>
  <TerminalScreen label={session.title} text={lines} />
</AgentPane>

components.a11y: The pane is a region named by its header title, so screen reader users can move between sessions by landmark. The tinted frame repeats what the header says in words: the state chip and the checked box. In forced colours the selected and blocked frames get a thicker system-coloured border. The terminal screen is a named group that takes focus, so it can be scrolled from the keyboard.

components.name: AgentPaneHeader
components.description: The title row of a pane: selection box, avatar, title, facts such as the branch, the state and the pane buttons. Pick it inside AgentPane; on a narrow pane the badges and buttons wrap instead of being cut.

examples.code:
<AgentPaneHeader
  title={session.title}
  onRename={rename}
  renameLabel={t('rename')}
  selectLabel={t('selectForBroadcast')}
  isSelected={picked}
  onSelectedChange={setPicked}
  avatar={<AgentAvatar letters="C" />}
  state={<SessionStateChip state="working" label={t('state.working')} />}
  actions={<IconButton size="sm" label={t('close')}><Icon name="action.close" /></IconButton>}
/>

components.a11y: The title is a heading (level 3 by default). With onRename it is a button that reads the title, then renameLabel; pressing it opens a text field, Enter or leaving saves, Escape cancels, and focus returns to the title. The selection box has its own name. Long titles are cut on screen and read in full. Every button is at least 24px.

components.name: AiDisclosure
components.description: The note that says a text was generated by a model: the words "AI generated", the model, the provider and a link to what is sent. Show it next to every answer or text a model wrote, in the assistant and in any other AI feature. It says where the text came from and nothing about how right it is.

examples.code:
<AiDisclosure
  label={t('ai.generated')}
  modelLabel={t('ai.model')}
  model="Example model 1"
  providerLabel={t('ai.provider')}
  provider="Example provider"
  sentLabel={t('ai.sent')}
  sentHref="/privacy#ai"
/>

components.a11y: A plain paragraph, so a screen reader reads the label, the model and the provider in order and the link is reachable with Tab. The label is a word, never only a colour or an icon. Every word is a prop, so the note is read in the language of the page. It wraps on narrow screens and keeps its contrast in all three themes.

components.name: Alert
components.description: A message inside the content, next to what it is about. Pick it for a result that stays on screen, such as the error summary at the top of a form; pick a toast for news that may pass.

examples.code: • Email address is missing

components.a11y: A static alert is a group named by its tone word and title. live="polite" makes it a status and live="assertive" (or urgent) an alert, so a message added after an action is read out; render the alert first and fill it later. headingLevel puts an error summary in the page outline, and links inside it can move focus to each field. The close button is a 24px or larger target and the message never closes on its own.

components.name: AlertRow
components.description: A record of an alert that happened, such as a crash or a failed health check, with where and when. Pick it for an alert history; Enter jumps to the source.

examples.code:
<List aria-label={t('alerts.recent')} items={alerts} emptyState={t('alerts.none')}>
  {(a) => <AlertRow id={a.id} tone={a.kind === 'unhealthy' ? 'warn' : 'danger'} toneLabel={t(`tone.${tone}`)}
    title={a.message} meta={`${a.project} · ${ago(a.at)}`} kindLabel={t(`alerts.${a.kind}`)}
    onAction={() => focus(a.containerId)} />}
</List>

components.a11y: Each tone has its own icon shape and is read as a word before the title. The row is history, not a live alert: announce a new alert with a toast, assertive when it blocks work. Enter runs onAction; meta and badges wrap at large zoom.

components.name: AppLayout
components.description: The page frame of the web apps: skip links, a sidebar, a top bar and the main column. Pick it for any signed-in screen; useAppLayout gives a custom control the same state as the menu button.

examples.code:
<AppLayout
  skipLinkLabel="Skip to content"
  skipToNavLabel="Skip to navigation"
  sidebar={<Sidebar label="Sidebar" closeLabel="Close navigation">…</Sidebar>}
  topbar={<Topbar menuLabel="Open navigation">…</Topbar>}
>
  <MainContent>…</MainContent>
</AppLayout>

components.a11y: The first Tab shows a skip link to the main landmark, and a second one to the navigation, which opens the sheet on a narrow layout. Below 48rem the sidebar becomes a modal sheet: focus moves in, stays in, and returns to the menu button on Escape. Set embedded for previews so the page keeps one set of landmarks.

components.name: AppLockup
components.description: The logo with Skribly and the tool name, for the title bar, the sidebar and sign-in pages. Give it href to make it the link home; compact keeps only the logo in a folded sidebar.

examples.code:
<AppLockup kind="agent" tool="Agent" href="/" />
<AppLockup kind="tracker" tool="Tracker" tone="nav" compact href="/" />

components.a11y: The words name it and the logo is hidden. As a link the whole lockup is the target, at least 24px high. label can give a fuller name, which should start with the visible words. compact hides the words on screen only, so the link keeps its name.

components.name: AppShell
components.description: The one shell of the Skribly apps, built from the parts below: the app switcher top left, a sidebar with For you and Recent, search that opens the CommandPalette, Create, a notifications slot for the Inbox, settings and the account. Pick it for every signed-in screen of Hub and the Tracker; every word is a prop, and linkComponent renders the links, so an app passes the link of its router, such as the one of Next.js, and the library imports no router.

props.name: notifications
props.type: { label: string; title: string; badge?: ReactNode; content: ReactNode }

props.name: account
props.type: { name: string description?: ReactNode avatarSrc?: string initials?: string links?: AppShellLink[] actions?: AppShellAction[] }

examples.code:
<AppShell
  labels={labels}
  apps={registryApps}
  currentAppId="tracker"
  forYou={[{ href: '/inbox', label: 'Inbox' }]}
  recent={recent}
  current={pathname}
  commands={commands}
  create={{ label: 'Create', onPress: openCreate }}
  notifications={{ label: 'Notifications, 2 new', title: 'Notifications', badge: 2, content: <Icon name="nav.inbox" compact … /> }}
  settings={{ label: 'Settings', href: '/settings' }}
  account={{ name, links: [{ href: '/profile', label: 'Profile' }], actions: [{ id: 'out', label: 'Sign out', onPress: signOut }] }}
  linkComponent={Link}
>
  <MainContent>…</MainContent>
</AppShell>

components.a11y: Tab goes through the skip links, the sidebar button, the app switcher, search, Create, notifications, settings and the account, then the sidebar links and the page. Ctrl+[ and Cmd+[ hide and show the sidebar; the button reports aria-expanded and a polite status says the new state. Below 48rem the same button and keys open the sidebar as a modal sheet. Search, Ctrl+K and Cmd+K open the command palette; Escape closes it and focus returns to where it was. The current app carries aria-current and a check mark, not colour alone. Every control is at least 44px on touch, and the shell holds at 320px with no sideways scroll: long names wrap or are cut with the full name in the panel.

components.name: AssistantWidget
components.description: A button that opens a dialog with a question field, the conversation and the AI note. The page passes an adapter with an ask function, the model, the provider and the link to what is sent. Every label is a prop. This demo uses a fake adapter with canned answers.

examples.code:
const adapter = {
  model: 'Example model 1',
  provider: 'Example provider',
  sentHref: '/privacy#ai',
  ask: async (question, { signal }) => ({ text: await callYourService(question, signal) })
}

<AssistantWidget adapter={adapter} labels={labels} />

components.a11y: The button is a real button that opens a real dialog: focus moves to the question field, stays inside while the dialog is open, and returns to the button on close. Escape closes it. The conversation is a log region, so each answer is read out as it arrives; sending, an empty question and an error are announced in a status region. Reduced motion and the panel's motion switch stop the opening animation. It works at 320 px.

components.name: AttachmentChips
components.description: The files attached to a message or a comment, with size, upload state and a remove button. Without onRemove it is a read-only list.

examples.code:
<AttachmentChips
  label="Attached files"
  items={files}
  onRemove={(ids) => remove(ids)}
  removeLabel="Remove"
/>

components.a11y: A tag group: Tab enters it, arrow keys move between files, and Delete or Backspace removes one. Each remove button is named by its verb and the file, such as "Remove notes.md, 2 KB". Long names are cut on screen and read in full. Upload and error states have an icon and a word.

components.name: AttentionItem
components.description: A short list of what needs the reader today: a count, what it is, why, and the way there. Mark blocking items urgent. When the list is empty, pass an empty state with the next step.

examples.code:
<AttentionList aria-label="Needs you">
  <AttentionItem count={3} label="Drafts" note="Waiting for review" href="/drafts" actionLabel="Review" />
  <AttentionItem count={1} label="Failed sync" urgent urgentLabel="Urgent" href="/sync" />
</AttentionList>

components.a11y: Each row is one link named by its count and label and described by the note, so a links list still makes sense. The whole row is the target and shows the focus ring. Urgent rows add a warning glyph and the urgentLabel word, never red alone. The action hint is hidden from screen readers.

components.name: AuthLayout
components.description: The frame of the sign in and password reset screens: a brand on top, one card with the page heading, and room for a language switch underneath. Use it for any short task a reader does before entering an app.

examples.code:

  <LoginForm labels={labels} aria-labelledby="auth-title" onSubmit={signIn} />
</AuthLayout>

components.name: Avatar
components.description: A person as initials or a photo, in lists, comments and assignee fields. With no name it draws the dashed unassigned circle.

examples.code:
<Avatar name="Anna Nowak" />
<Avatar name="Jan Kowalski" src={user.photo} size="lg" />
<Avatar unassignedLabel="Unassigned" />

components.a11y: An image named after the person. Set decorative when the name is written next to it, so it is not read twice. The unassigned circle is read only with unassignedLabel. A photo that fails to load falls back to the initials.

components.name: Badge
components.description: A short label for a state or a count, such as Draft or Failed. Pick it for static facts inside rows and headers; use StatusDot when the state is live.

examples.code: <Badge tone="ok" icon={<Check />}>Done</Badge>

components.a11y: Plain text, so screen readers read the word. Icons are hidden. Every tone pairs its colour with text, and the text and tint pairs meet 4.5:1 in all three themes. Long text truncates on screen and stays whole for screen readers; pass title when the full text matters. A transparent border keeps the outline in forced colours.

components.name: Banner
components.description: A full-width strip at the top of a page or panel for a state that lasts, such as read-only mode or a lost connection.

examples.code:
<Banner tone="warn" toneLabel={t('tone.warning')} title="Read-only mode" sticky actions={<Button size="sm">Renew</Button>}>
  Changes are not saved until the plan is renewed.
</Banner>

components.a11y: A region named by its tone word and title, so it is listed with the landmarks. Set live when the banner appears after the page loads, such as on losing the connection. Actions wrap under the text on narrow screens. The close button only hides it; the state it reports stays until it is fixed.

components.name: BarChart
components.description: Counts per day as columns, or a ranking as rows. Pick columns for a count over time and flag the days that need a look; pick rows for top lists, where names can be long and the screen narrow.

examples.code:
<LineChart {...props} isLoading loadingLabel="Loading visits" />
<LineChart {...props} error="The report could not be loaded. Try again in a minute." />
<BarChart {...props} data={[]} emptyState="No errors in this period." />

<BarChart
  label="Errors per day"
  valueLabel="Errors"
  data={days.map((day) => ({ id: day.iso, label: day.long, axisLabel: day.short, value: day.errors, highlight: day.errors > 30 }))}
  highlightLabel="Spike"
  keyboardHint="Use the arrow keys to read each day."
  table={{ trigger: 'Show as table', categoryHeader: 'Date' }}
/>

<BarChart orientation="rows" ordered label="Top pages" valueLabel="Visits" data={pages} />

components.a11y:
Loading is a status that is read politely and marks the figure busy. An error is an alert with an icon and words, read at once. The empty state is plain text with an icon. None of them relies on colour, and the spinner stops under reduced motion.

Columns work like the line chart: one tab stop, arrow keys, Home and End, a polite live region, Escape to hide the tooltip, and a table of every value. A highlighted column has a marker above it and its meaning in the legend, the tooltip and what is read, so the flag does not rest on the colour. Rows are a plain list with every name and value in text; the bars are hidden from screen readers. Rows wrap their names and put the bar on its own line in a narrow box.

components.name: Board
components.description: The Kanban board of a project: a column per status, cards that move between them, and a voice that says how the move went. The board is controlled; apply onMove with moveBoardCards and save it. Turn on "Fail the next save" to see the error path.

examples.code:
<BoardAnnouncer message={message} />
<Board aria-label={t('board.title')} columns={columns} labels={labels}
  onMove={(move) => { setColumns((c) => moveBoardCards(c, move)); save(move) }} />

<Board aria-label={t('board.title')} columns={columns} labels={labels} isReadOnly />
<Board aria-label={t('board.title')} columns={[]} labels={labels} error={t('board.failed')} />

components.a11y:
Each column is a section named by its heading, holding a React Aria GridList: one tab stop per column, arrow keys between cards, typeahead by key and title. Cards move by pointer drag, by keyboard and screen reader through the drag handle (Enter, then arrows and Enter, with React Aria’s spoken instructions), and by the move menu, the one-pointer way to move that WCAG 2.5.7 asks for. Focus follows a card that the menu moved. BoardAnnouncer reads saved moves politely and failed ones assertively, and its visible message stays until the next one. Over a work in progress limit the count gains a warning glyph and overLimit words. Columns stack below 48rem and scroll in their own box above it.

A read-only board drops the drag handles and menus, and cards still open the issue. Loading is a status with a spinner and words, and sets aria-busy; an error is an assertive alert with a glyph, since nothing else on the board works.

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.description: Shows where a page sits and links to each level above it. With moreLabel set, long trails fold their middle levels into a menu.

examples.code:
<Breadcrumbs label="Breadcrumb" moreLabel="Show hidden levels" items={[
  { id: 'home', label: 'Home', href: '/' },
  { id: 'docs', label: 'Docs', href: '/docs' },
  { id: 'install', label: 'Install' }
]} />

components.a11y: A nav landmark with an ordered list; the last item is the current page with aria-current="page". The fold button opens a menu of the hidden levels, navigable with arrow keys and closed with Escape. Separators are hidden from screen readers. Items wrap on narrow screens and long labels truncate while keeping their full name.

components.name: BrowserBar
components.description: A page preview: back, forward, reload or stop, the address and the preview size, over a frame that simulates a screen width. Pick it for previewing a site while working on it; the frame holds an iframe in an app.

examples.code:
<BrowserBar label={t('preview.controls')} addressLabel={t('preview.address')}
  address={address} onAddressChange={setAddress} onNavigate={go}
  backLabel={t('nav.back')} forwardLabel={t('nav.forward')} reloadLabel={t('nav.reload')}
  onBack={back} onReload={reload} canGoBack={canGoBack} isLoading={loading} loadingLabel={t('preview.loading')}
  devices={devices} device={device} onDeviceChange={setDevice} deviceLabel={t('preview.size')} />
<DeviceFrame label={t('preview.page')} width={820} caption="Tablet · 820 px" isLoading={loading}
  loadingLabel={t('preview.loading')}>
  <iframe title={t('preview.page')} src={url} />
</DeviceFrame>

components.a11y: The bar is a named group of buttons with names and tooltips, an address form (Enter navigates, focus selects the text) and a radio group of sizes whose names are read and shown in words on wide bars. Back and forward turn off when there is nowhere to go. The frame is a named region; loading shows a named spinner, and an error replaces the page as an assertive alert with an icon and a word. The frame never grows past its box and its width change stops under reduced motion.

components.name: BulkActionBar
components.description: An interactive grid for records people select, sort and open: a sticky header, numeric and action columns, and a selected row marked with a tint and a leading rule. BulkActionBar sits above it and acts on the selection.

examples.code:
<BulkActionBar aria-label="Actions for selected releases" count={count}
  countLabel={(n) => `${n} selected`} onClear={clear} clearLabel="Clear selection">
  <Button variant="danger" size="sm" onPress={remove}>Delete</Button>
</BulkActionBar>
<DataTable
  aria-label="Releases"
  className="max-h-72"
  columns={columns}
  items={releases}
  rowKey={(i) => i.id}
  selectionMode="multiple"
  selectedKeys={selected}
  onSelectionChange={setSelected}
  sortDescriptor={sort}
  onSortChange={setSort}
/>

components.a11y: Tab enters the grid once; arrow keys move between cells, Space toggles a row, Enter opens it when onRowAction is set, and typing jumps to a row. Column headers sort with Enter and React Aria announces the new order. Row checkboxes are named after the row header. The bulk bar is a toolbar with one tab stop and arrow keys between its actions; its buttons disable while nothing is selected, and focus moves to the count when an action empties the selection.

components.name: Button
components.description: The default way to run an action. Use primary for the one main action of a view, outline or ghost for the rest, danger for removal and danger-solid only to confirm something that cannot be undone.

props.name: children
props.type: ReactNode | ((values: ButtonRenderProps & { defaultChildren: ReactNode | undefined }) => ReactNode)

examples.code:
<Button onPress={save} isPending={saving} pendingLabel="Saving">
  <Icon name="action.save" aria-hidden />
  Save changes
</Button>
<Button variant="danger">Remove</Button>

components.a11y: A native button: Tab to reach it, Enter or Space to press. While pending it keeps focus, ignores presses, stops form submission and is read with its pending label. Disabled buttons leave the tab order; when a person needs to know why, use GatedAction. Long labels wrap rather than overflow, and every variant keeps a border so it stays visible in Windows high contrast.

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.description: Keeps related buttons together. Spaced for sets of separate actions, attached for a segmented look, toolbar for a strip of tools, and stackOnNarrow for form footers that should go full width on a phone.

examples.code:
<ButtonGroup label="Formatting" toolbar attached>
  <ToggleButton aria-label="Bold"><Icon name="format.bold" aria-hidden /></ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton aria-label="Italic"><Icon name="format.italic" aria-hidden /></ToggleButton>
</ButtonGroup>

components.a11y: A plain group has role="group" and label as its name; every button keeps its own Tab stop. A toolbar is one Tab stop: Left and Right (Up and Down when vertical) move between buttons, mirrored in right-to-left text. Groups wrap at narrow widths instead of scrolling.

components.name: Card
components.description: A bordered surface for one block of content. Use the header, body and footer parts for a titled panel with actions; use the card alone with padding for a simple box.

examples.code:
<Card as="section" padding="none">
  <CardHeader actions={<Button size="sm" variant="outline">Add</Button>}>
    <CardTitle icon={<Icon name="vcs.repository" />}>Projects</CardTitle>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardBody>…</CardBody>
  <CardFooter><Button variant="ghost">Open all</Button></CardFooter>
</Card>

components.a11y: As a section, article or aside the card becomes a region named by its CardTitle. Pick the heading level that fits the page outline with level. The title icon is hidden from screen readers. Header actions wrap under the title on narrow screens, and long titles break instead of overflowing.

components.name: ChartLegend
components.description: The key and the point readout every chart here uses, for a custom chart that should look the same. Pick ChartLegend whenever colour stands for more than one thing.

examples.code:
<ChartLegend
  label="Series"
  items={[
    { id: 'visits', label: 'Visits', color: 1, shape: 'line' },
    { id: 'previous', label: 'Previous period', color: 'muted', shape: 'line', pattern: 'short' }
  ]}
/>
<ChartTooltip title="14 March 2026" items={[{ id: 'visits', label: 'Visits', value: '1,602', color: 1, shape: 'line' }]} />

components.a11y: The legend is a list named by label; each swatch is hidden and the name is text. Line swatches carry the same dash pattern as their line, so they match without colour. The tooltip never takes the pointer, keeps to the box near its edges and wraps long text. Inside a chart it is hidden from screen readers, because the same words are read through the live region; on its own it is plain text.

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: A Checkbox is one yes or no answer saved with the form, such as accepting terms. A CheckboxGroup is several independent choices under one label.

examples.code:
<CheckboxGroup label="Notify me about" defaultValue={['mentions']}>
  <Checkbox value="mentions">Mentions</Checkbox>
  <Checkbox value="reviews">Review requests</Checkbox>
</CheckboxGroup>

components.a11y: Space toggles; the label is part of the target, so the row clears 24px. Checked shows a tick and indeterminate shows a dash, both kept in forced colours. A group has one label, one description and one error for the set.

components.name: Checklist
components.description: A list of what has to happen before something is ready, with a link to fix each item. Items can show state from data, or be checkboxes the reader ticks for a manual list.

examples.code:
<Checklist title="Ready to go live" doneLabel="done" todoLabel="to do"
  progressLabel={(done, total) => `${done} of ${total} done`}>
  <ChecklistItem title="Logo" hint="Shown in the header." actionLabel="Fix" href="/settings/logo" />
</Checklist>

components.a11y: A region named by its title, with the count in words. Data rows read "done" or "to do" after the title and show a check or an empty circle; tickable rows are real checkboxes with the hint as description. "Fix" links are named with their item. Hints and links disappear once an item is done.

components.description: A list of what has to happen before something is ready, with a link to fix each item. Items can show state from data, or be checkboxes the reader ticks for a manual list.

examples.code:

  progressLabel={(done, total) => `${done} of ${total} done`}>

</Checklist>

components.a11y: A region named by its title, with the count in words. components.name: ChipCount
components.description: A small count next to a label: unread items, open issues or results. It caps long numbers, such as 99+.

examples.code:
<FilterChips label="Status" selected={status} onChange={setStatus} clearLabel="Clear filters"
  chips={[{ id: 'open', label: 'Open', count: 42, countLabel: '42 issues' }]} />
<ChipCount value={1280} max={999} label="1280 issues" />
<ChipCount value={250} label="250 unread" />

components.a11y:
Multiple mode is a set of toggle buttons with aria-pressed; single mode is a radio group. An active chip gains a check mark and an accent border, so the state never rests on colour. Counts read as their label, such as "42 issues". The clear button returns focus to the chips once it goes away. Chips wrap on narrow screens.

The number is read as the label when one is given, so a screen reader hears "250 unread" rather than "99 plus". It keeps a border under forced colours.

components.name: ChipInput
components.description: Free text that turns into removable chips, such as topics or email addresses. For a fixed list of options, use MultiSelect.

examples.code:
<ChipInput label="Topics" removeLabel="Remove" defaultValue={['design']}
  duplicateMessage={(chip) => `"${chip}" is already in the list`} />

components.a11y: Enter or a comma adds a chip, and pasting a list splits it. The chips are one tab stop: arrow keys move, Delete or Backspace removes, and each remove button reads "Remove" and the chip. Backspace in the empty box moves to the last chip; a duplicate raises a polite warning.

components.name: ClosableTabs
components.description: A strip of open documents or pages that the reader can close, as in an editor or a browser. A dot marks unsaved changes and turns into the close button on hover or focus.

examples.code:
<ClosableTabs label="Open files" items={files} selectedId={active} onSelect={setActive}
  onClose={close} closeLabel="Close" dirtyLabel="unsaved changes" emptyLabel="No open files" />

components.a11y: Arrow keys move between tabs, Enter or Space opens one, Delete or Backspace closes the focused tab and focus moves to its neighbour. Each close button is a real 24px button named with the tab, such as "Close App.tsx", so pointer and touch screen readers reach it. Unsaved state is read as part of the tab name, not shown by the dot alone.

components.name: CloseButton
components.description: Closes or dismisses the thing it sits in: a notice, a panel or a dialog. Inside a React Aria Dialog, slot="close" closes it with no handler.

examples.code:
<CloseButton label="Dismiss export notice" onPress={dismiss} />
<CloseButton slot="close" label="Close dialog" />

components.a11y: Name it after what closes, such as "Close settings", so a list of buttons read out of context still makes sense. When it removes the element that had focus, move focus somewhere sensible, as the demo does with the button that brings the notice back.

components.name: CodeBlock
components.description: Shows a block of code with an optional file name, language tag, line numbers and copy button. Pick Snippet for a single command.

examples.code:
<CodeBlock
  code={source}
  label="Example: Save button"
  title="Save.tsx"
  language="tsx"
  copyLabel="Copy"
  copiedLabel="Copied"
  copyFailedLabel="Could not copy"
/>

components.a11y: The code area is a named group in the tab order, so keyboard users can scroll it. Line numbers are hidden from screen readers and from selection. The copy result shows as an icon and a word, and a polite status region reads it out. It stays while the pointer or focus is on the button.

components.name: ColorInput
components.description: A colour as a hex value, typed or picked. Presets keep choices within a palette, such as label or brand colours.

examples.code:
<ColorInput label="Label colour" pickerLabel="Pick a colour" hueLabel="Hue"
  defaultValue="#d97706" swatches={['#d97706', '#2563eb']} swatchesLabel="Presets" />

components.a11y: The hex field accepts typing and arrow keys. The swatch button opens a dialog with a 2D colour area, a hue slider and presets, all keyboard operable; the presets are a listbox named by the required swatchesLabel, and React Aria names each colour in words. The hex text says the value, so the swatch is never the only cue.

components.name: CommandList
components.description: The slash commands of an agent behind a search field. Pick it in a ToolbarMenu or beside a composer, wherever the user picks one command to type into the session.

examples.code:
<CommandList
  commands={toolbox.commands}
  searchLabel={t('searchCommands')}
  listLabel={t('commands')}
  emptyLabel={(q) => t('noCommand', { q })}
  onRun={(c) => send('/' + c.name)}
/>

components.a11y: React Aria’s Autocomplete with a menu: the field keeps focus while arrow keys move through the matches, each row is read as it is reached with its description, and Enter runs it. The number of matches is read politely as the query changes. Names that start with the query come first. Long descriptions wrap to two lines and are read in full.

components.name: CommandPalette
components.description: One search for every view and action of an app, opened with Cmd K or Ctrl K. Pick it for apps with many places to go; use GlobalSearch for content.

examples.code:
<CommandPalette isOpen={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} shortcut commands={commands}
  label="Command palette" searchLabel="Search commands" listLabel="Commands" closeLabel="Close"
  emptyLabel={(q) => `Nothing matches “${q}”.`}
  recentLabel="Recent" recentKey="my-app-recent" />

components.a11y: A modal dialog: focus starts in the search field, stays inside while open and returns to the trigger on close. Typing filters by label, hint and keywords in a fuzzy way, with the matched letters marked. Up and Down move, Enter runs, Escape clears the field and then closes. Commands are menu items named by their label and then their hint, with the shortcut as key caps; disabled ones are announced as such. On narrow screens it becomes a full-screen sheet with a close button.

components.name: CommentForm
components.description: Writes a Markdown comment with a preview, checks it is not empty, and shows posting, posted and failed states. Pick it under a comment thread or to edit a comment.

examples.code:
<CommentForm
  label="Add a comment"
  writeLabel="Write"
  previewLabel="Preview"
  emptyPreview="Nothing to preview yet."
  submitLabel="Comment"
  requiredMessage="Write a comment first."
  successMessage="Comment posted."
  failedMessage="Not posted. Try again."
  onSubmit={(text) => api.comment(text)}
/>

components.a11y: An empty post moves focus to the text area, sets aria-invalid and links the message with aria-describedby. Success is a polite status that stays until you type again; failure is an alert, read out at once, and the text is kept. Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter posts from the text area.

components.name: CommentItem
components.description: One comment in a thread, with avatar, author, a badge, time, edited mark and actions. Put the comments of a thread in an ordered list.
components.a11y: Each comment is an article named by its author. The avatar is decorative, because the name is in the text. A link to the comment highlights it with a border and a fill, not only colour. Failed states are read out at once.

components.name: CommitBox
components.description: The top of a changes panel: branch, push and pull with counts, the message and the commit button, with room for suggestion tools and a ReasonList that explains a suggested message. Try committing a short message to see the inline error.

examples.code:
<CommitBox label={t('commit.box')} messageLabel={t('commit.message')} hideMessageLabel
  value={message} onChange={setMessage} onCommit={commit} commitLabel={t('commit.do')}
  errorMessage={error} branch={status.branch} branchLabel={t('git.switchBranch')} onBranchPress={openBranches}
  ahead={status.ahead} onPush={push} pushLabel={t('git.push')} syncing={syncing} syncingLabel={t('git.syncing')}
  container={panel} footer={proposal && <ReasonList title={proposal.template} reasons={proposal.reasons}
    alternatives={proposal.alternatives} onPickAlternative={setMessage} />} />

components.a11y: The box is a named group. The message is a labelled textarea: Enter adds a line and Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter commits. An error marks the field invalid and is linked with aria-describedby, so it is read with the field and stays until the message changes. Push reads as "Push 2", busy buttons say they are pending, and the ReasonList is a group named by its title with real list items and buttons for alternatives.

components.name: ComposeBar
components.description: The compose files of a project with their commands. One command runs at a time, and Down asks first. Pick it above a list of containers.

examples.code:
<ComposeBar title={t('docker.compose')} files={files} actions={[
    { id: 'up', label: 'Up', icon: <Icon name="media.play" aria-hidden />, variant: 'primary' },
    { id: 'down', label: 'Down', variant: 'danger', confirm: { title: t('docker.downTitle'),
      body: t('docker.downBody'), confirmLabel: t('docker.down'), cancelLabel: t('common.cancel') } }
  ]} onAction={run} pending={pending} pendingLabel={t('common.running')} />

components.a11y: A section named by its heading. The buttons of each file are a group named by the file, so "Up" is never ambiguous. The running button says it is pending and the others wait. Down opens an alert dialog with focus on Cancel. Buttons wrap under the file name on a narrow card.

components.name: Composer
components.description: The message box under a chat: it grows with the text, sends on Enter, attaches files by button, paste or drop, and turns into a stop button while the agent answers. Pick CommentForm for longer Markdown posts.

examples.code:
<Composer
  label="Message to Claude Code"
  sendLabel="Send"
  onSubmit={send}
  isBusy={busy}
  stop={{ label: 'Stop', onStop: stop }}
  attach={{ label: 'Attach files', dropLabel: 'Drop to attach', onFiles: add }}
  attachments={<AttachmentChips … />}
/>

components.a11y: The text area has a label, hidden on screen unless showLabel, and the hint and error are linked with aria-describedby. Enter sends unless an input method is composing; Shift+Enter adds a line. Every button has a name. Dropping files is an extra: the attach button and paste do the same by keyboard.

components.name: ConfirmDialog
components.description: Asks before an action that is hard to undo. It waits for an async action, shows the pending state and keeps the dialog open with an error if the action fails.

examples.code:
<ConfirmDialog
  tone="danger"
  trigger={<Button variant="danger">Delete</Button>}
  title="Delete this draft?"
  confirmLabel="Delete draft"
  cancelLabel="Keep it"
  error={error}
  onConfirm={remove}
>
  This cannot be undone.
</ConfirmDialog>

components.a11y: An alertdialog. A destructive action starts focus on Cancel, any other on the action, so Enter does the safe thing. The danger tone has a warning icon and says what happens in words. An error is announced at once with role="alert". Escape is ignored while the action runs.

components.name: ConnectionCard
components.description: A connected account or service: who, its state, a quiet detail and actions. Pick it for Git hosts, trackers or any integration settings.

examples.code:
<ConnectionCard avatar={<VcsBadge kind={a.kind} size={36} />} name={a.name} handle={`@${a.login}`}
  status={a.hasSecret ? { tone: 'ok', label: t('accounts.connected') } : { tone: 'warn', label: t('accounts.noToken') }}
  detail={a.url} actions={<Button size="sm" onPress={() => browse(a)}>{t('accounts.repositories')}</Button>} />

components.a11y: An article named by its heading. The state is a badge with an icon and a word. While checking, the card sets aria-busy and shows a named spinner. Long addresses wrap anywhere, and the actions move under the text on a narrow card.

components.name: ContainerRow
components.description: One container with its state, image, uptime, ports, usage and actions. Pick it for a list of containers or services; the demo changes state, shows a busy row and confirms with a polite message.

examples.code:
<List aria-label={t('docker.containers')} items={containers} emptyState={t('docker.none')}>
  {(c) => (
    <ContainerRow id={c.id} name={c.service} secondaryName={c.name} state={runState(c)}
      stateLabel={t(`docker.state.${runState(c)}`)} image={c.image} status={c.status}
      ports={c.ports.map((p) => ({ host: p.hostPort, container: p.containerPort, href: url(p), label: t('docker.openPort') }))}
      isBusy={busy === c.id} busyLabel={t('docker.working', { name: c.service })}
      actions={<IconButton label={t('docker.restart', { name: c.service })} size="sm" onPress={() => restart(c)}><Icon name="action.retry" aria-hidden /></IconButton>} />
  )}
</List>

components.a11y: The list is one tab stop; arrow keys move between containers and Right reaches the links and buttons in a row. The state is a shaped glyph and a word, never colour alone. Port links start their name with what is seen. A busy row shows a named spinner and its buttons wait. Actions wrap under the text on a narrow row, and every button clears 24px.

components.name: ContextStat
components.description: Small read-only figures for a session: time, context used and subagents. Pick ToolbarStat for any other figure; the three others format their value and switch tone on their own.

examples.code:
<SessionClock label={t('time')} since={session.startedAt} />
<ContextStat label={t('context')} tokens={48210} window={200000} />
<SubagentStat label={t('subagents')} count={3} running={1} runningLabel={(n) => t('running', { n })} />
<ToolbarStat label={t('toolCalls')} value="14" icon={<Wrench />} />

components.a11y: Each figure reads its label before the value, such as "Context: 48K · 24%". The clock is a timer, which screen readers do not announce on every tick. Near the limit ContextStat switches to a warning icon as well as a warning tint, and the percentage says the same; SubagentStat says how many run in words. Figures are text and take no focus.

components.name: CopyButton
components.description: Copies a command, key or link to the clipboard and confirms it. Use it next to text people are likely to paste elsewhere.

examples.code:
<CopyButton
  text="npm run build"
  label="Copy"
  copiedLabel="Copied"
  failedLabel="Copy failed. Select the text and press Ctrl+C."
/>

components.a11y: Success and failure each have an icon and a word and are announced through a polite live region. The confirmation stays while the button is hovered or focused and goes back afterwards; a failure stays on screen, with what to do instead, until the next press. The icon-only form keeps a stable name.

components.name: DataTable
components.description: The full grid of an admin panel on 2,000 posts: search, faceted filters with chips, sort by several columns (Shift with a click adds the next key), columns to hide, reorder and resize, two densities, selection with bulk actions, a menu on every row, thumbnails and badges, pages with a page size, CSV export of the view, and the view kept in the address. Switch the source to a server to see paging and a skeleton while the next page loads, and choose All rows to render only the rows in view.

examples.code:
<BulkActionBar aria-label="Actions for selected releases" count={count}
  countLabel={(n) => `${n} selected`} onClear={clear} clearLabel="Clear selection">
  <Button variant="danger" size="sm" onPress={remove}>Delete</Button>
</BulkActionBar>
<DataTable
  aria-label="Releases"
  className="max-h-72"
  columns={columns}
  items={releases}
  rowKey={(i) => i.id}
  selectionMode="multiple"
  selectedKeys={selected}
  onSelectionChange={setSelected}
  sortDescriptor={sort}
  onSortChange={setSort}
/>

<DataTable aria-label="Releases" columns={columns} items={[]} rowKey={(i) => i.id}
  isLoading={isLoading} loadingLabel="Loading releases"
  error={failed ? 'Could not load releases.' : undefined}
  emptyState="No releases match these filters." />

components.a11y:
One tab stop enters the grid; arrow keys move between cells, Home and End along a row, Space selects a row, and typing jumps to a row. A header sorts on Enter or a click and only the main sort key carries aria-sort; further keys show their position and say it in words. Column edges are separators the arrow keys resize. The toolbar fields and menus are named, the filter chips each have a remove button, and the count of matching rows is read politely after a search. The row header column and the header stay in view while the box scrolls. Loading is a status, an error an alert with its retry button, and every state is said in words.

Tab enters the grid once; arrow keys move between cells, Space toggles a row, Enter opens it when onRowAction is set, and typing jumps to a row. Column headers sort with Enter and React Aria announces the new order. Row checkboxes are named after the row header. The bulk bar is a toolbar with one tab stop and arrow keys between its actions; its buttons disable while nothing is selected, and focus moves to the count when an action empties the selection.

Loading is a polite status with a spinner that stops under reduced motion. An error is an assertive alert with an icon and its own words, never colour alone. The empty state may hold a button, which stays reachable inside the grid.

components.name: DateInput
components.description: A day, typed segment by segment or picked in a calendar, such as a due date. The order of day, month and year follows the locale.

examples.code: <DateInput label="Due date" defaultValue={parseDate('2026-11-20')} />

components.a11y: Each segment is a spin button: type digits or use the arrow keys, and Tab moves on. The calendar button opens a dialog where arrow keys move by day, Page Up and Page Down by month. Today is bold and underlined; the chosen day is filled.

components.name: DateTimeInput
components.description: A day and a time in one field, such as a reminder or a release. Pass a ZonedDateTime to show the time zone.

examples.code: <DateTimeInput label="Remind me" defaultValue={parseDateTime('2026-11-20T09:30')} />

components.a11y: The hour and minute segments take digits or arrow keys; the hour cycle follows the locale unless hourCycle is set. The calendar stays open after picking a day, so the time can be checked before closing with Escape.

components.name: Delta
components.description: The change of a figure against an earlier period, with its direction and whether that is good news. Pick it beside a headline number, in a tile or a table.

examples.code:
<Delta
  value={0.224}
  directionLabels={{ up: 'Up', down: 'Down', flat: 'No change' }}
  assessmentLabels={{ good: 'better', bad: 'worse' }}
  comparison="vs previous 28 days"
/>

components.a11y: The arrow is hidden and the direction is read as a word before the number. Good and bad are a colour and, with assessmentLabels, a word for screen readers, so nothing rests on colour alone; the text colours meet 4.5:1 in every theme. The comparison wraps under the number in a narrow box.

components.name: DeviceFrame
components.description: A page preview: back, forward, reload or stop, the address and the preview size, over a frame that simulates a screen width. Pick it for previewing a site while working on it; the frame holds an iframe in an app.

examples.code:
<BrowserBar label={t('preview.controls')} addressLabel={t('preview.address')}
  address={address} onAddressChange={setAddress} onNavigate={go}
  backLabel={t('nav.back')} forwardLabel={t('nav.forward')} reloadLabel={t('nav.reload')}
  onBack={back} onReload={reload} canGoBack={canGoBack} isLoading={loading} loadingLabel={t('preview.loading')}
  devices={devices} device={device} onDeviceChange={setDevice} deviceLabel={t('preview.size')} />
<DeviceFrame label={t('preview.page')} width={820} caption="Tablet · 820 px" isLoading={loading}
  loadingLabel={t('preview.loading')}>
  <iframe title={t('preview.page')} src={url} />
</DeviceFrame>

components.a11y: The bar is a named group of buttons with names and tooltips, an address form (Enter navigates, focus selects the text) and a radio group of sizes whose names are read and shown in words on wide bars. Back and forward turn off when there is nowhere to go. The frame is a named region; loading shows a named spinner, and an error replaces the page as an assertive alert with an icon and a word. The frame never grows past its box and its width change stops under reduced motion.

components.name: Divider
components.description: A line between groups of content, across or upright, with an optional word such as Or in the middle.

examples.code:
<Divider />
<Divider label="Or" />
<Divider orientation="vertical" />

components.a11y: A plain divider is a separator with its orientation. A labelled one reads its word as text and hides the lines. Lines are borders, so they stay visible in Windows high contrast.

components.name: Dock
components.description: The frame of the desktop app: a title bar, an activity bar, a status bar and a dock for a side panel such as the agent chat. Pick Dock for a panel that sits beside any view and can be resized or closed.

examples.code:
<AppLayout skipLinkLabel="Skip to content" titlebar={<Titlebar brand={…} actions={…} />}
  activityBar={<ActivityBar label="Views">…</ActivityBar>} statusBar={<StatusBar label="Status">…</StatusBar>}>
  <MainContent>…</MainContent>
  <Dock label="Agent panel" closeLabel="Close" onClose={close} resizeLabel="Resize the agent panel">…</Dock>
</AppLayout>

components.a11y: The title bar is the banner and the dock a named complementary landmark with a level 2 heading. Its grip is a focusable separator: arrow keys resize by 16px, Home and End go to the limits, Enter collapses and restores. Below 48rem the dock opens as a modal sheet that closes on Escape; on a phone this demo starts with it closed, so the page is not hidden behind a sheet nobody opened.

components.name: DockGrip
components.description: The resize handle on the edge of a panel, such as a terminal under the editor. Dock adds one itself; use DockGrip directly for a panel of your own.

examples.code:
<section id="terminal" style={{ height }} className="relative">
  <DockGrip label="Resize the terminal" value={height} onChange={setHeight} minValue={80} maxValue={400} edge="top" controls="terminal" />
</section>

components.a11y: A focusable separator named by its label, with its size reported as a percent of the range. Arrow keys move it by 16px, Page Up and Page Down by 160px, Home and End to the limits, Enter collapses and restores. The hit area is 12px wide along the whole edge.

components.name: DonutChart
components.description: The share of a whole across a few parts, such as visits by device. Pick it for up to five parts; past that, the smallest fold into one "other" slice, and a bar chart may read better.

examples.code:
<DonutChart
  label="Visits by device"
  slices={[
    { id: 'desktop', label: 'Desktop', value: 18_204 },
    { id: 'mobile', label: 'Mobile', value: 9_871 },
    { id: 'tablet', label: 'Tablet', value: 1_204 }
  ]}
  centerLabel="visits"
  otherLabel="Other"
/>

components.a11y: The ring is decoration. The legend beside it is a list with every share, name and value in text, and the total sits in the hole as text. Pointing at a slice or an entry lights up both, as an extra; nothing is only on hover. Slices are split by a gap that stays in forced colours. In a narrow box the legend wraps under the ring.

components.name: DragHandle
components.description: The grip that drags an item in a sortable React Aria GridList, Table or Tree. Always pair dragging with a second way to reorder, such as NudgeButtons, for people who cannot drag.

examples.code:
<GridListItem textValue={page.name}>
  <DragHandle label={`Drag ${page.name}`} />
  {page.name}
</GridListItem>

components.a11y: The handle fills the drag slot of the item, so React Aria gives it keyboard dragging (Enter to pick up, arrows to choose a place, Enter to drop, Escape to cancel) and reads the instructions and the drop position aloud. The target is 24px square even though the grip is smaller.

components.name: DropdownMenu
components.description: A list of actions behind a button. MenuItem rows take an icon, a description, a shortcut and a danger tone; pick a menu for commands, not for choosing a form value.

examples.code:
<DropdownMenu trigger={<IconButton label="Help"><Icon name="status.help" /></IconButton>} onAction={run}>
  <MenuItem id="guide" icon={<Icon name="nav.help" />}>Start the guide</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem id="delete" tone="danger">Delete</MenuItem>
</DropdownMenu>

components.a11y: Enter, Space or Arrow Down opens it on the first row, Arrow Up on the last. Arrows move, typing jumps to a row, Enter runs it and Escape closes. The menu is named by its trigger, each row by all of its text, label first, so a description is read with it, and icons are hidden. Rows are at least 32px tall.

components.name: EditorStatusBar
components.description: The bar under a code editor: caret position as a "go to line" button, selection, unsaved state, language, encoding and line endings.

examples.code:
<EditorStatusBar label={t('editor.status')} position={t('editor.position', cursor)}
  onPositionPress={goToLine} positionTip={t('editor.goToLine')} isDirty={tab.dirty}
  unsavedLabel={t('editor.unsaved')} facts={[{ id: 'lang', label: language }, { id: 'eol', label: 'LF' }]} />

components.a11y: A named group rather than a footer landmark, so several editors add no landmarks. The caret position is not live, as it changes with every key; the unsaved state is announced once through a polite region and shown with a warning glyph and its word. Buttons show tips on hover and keyboard focus and clear 24px; items wrap on a narrow pane.

components.name: EffortChips
components.description: One choice among a few levels, such as how hard a model thinks. Pick it for three to six short options that fit on one line; use a Select for more.

examples.code: <EffortChips label={t('effort')} levels={levels} value={effort} onChange={setEffort} defaultLabel={t('default')} />

components.a11y: A radio group from React Aria: Tab enters at the chosen chip, arrow keys move between chips, Space or Enter picks one, and the group reads its label. The chosen chip shows a tick as well as a tint, and a system highlight border in forced colours. Chips wrap on a narrow screen and are at least 24px tall.

components.name: EmptyState
components.description: What fills a view that has nothing to show: nothing yet, no results, or could not load. Always give the next step, such as creating the first item, clearing filters or trying again.

examples.code:
<EmptyState
  icon={<Icon name="nav.inbox" />}
  title="No projects yet"
  description="Projects keep your files and tasks together."
  actions={<Button>New project</Button>}
/>

components.a11y: The title is a real heading; set headingLevel to fit the page outline. The icon is hidden. The danger tone is for failures, and its title says what failed, so the colour is never the only sign. Text wraps and centres at any width.

components.name: ErrorPage
components.description: A full page for 404, 403, 500 and 503: what happened in plain words and the ways out. Children add a second language, a request id or a search box.

examples.code:
<ErrorPage
  code={404}
  codeLabel="Error"
  title="Page not found"
  description="The address may be mistyped."
  actions={<LinkButton href="/" variant="primary">Go to the start page</LinkButton>}
/>

Try again}>

Request id: {requestId}

components.a11y:
The large number is decoration; the heading reads "Error 404. Page not found". Text in another language carries its lang attribute. In a single page app, focusOnMount moves focus to the heading so screen readers hear the error. The actions stack full width on a phone.

Retry is a real button and keeps focus; the request id wraps instead of widening the page at 320px.

components.name: FaviconLetter
components.description: A site icon with a letter fallback, for browser tabs, bookmarks and link lists. The letter is the first one of the host, without www.

examples.code: <FaviconLetter site="https://www.example.com" src="https://www.example.com/favicon.ico" />

components.a11y: Decoration by default, because the page title is written next to it. A favicon that fails to load falls back to the letter. Its size is in rem and follows the text size.

components.name: Field
components.description: Label, help, status and error around a control that is not one of this group, such as a native element or a widget from another library. Pick a ready field such as TextField when one fits.

examples.code:
<Field label="Website" description="Shown on your profile." errorMessage={error}>
  {(control) => <input {...control} type="url" className="…" />}
</Field>

components.a11y: The render function gets id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid and aria-required, so the label names the control and the help, status and error are read after it. The asterisk is hidden from screen readers, which hear "required" from aria-required. The status is an output element, a polite live region.

components.name: FileInput
components.description: Attach files by picking, dropping or pasting them. It checks type and size and lists what was chosen with a remove button each.

examples.code:
<FileInput label="Attachments" buttonLabel="Choose files" dropLabel="or drop them here"
  removeLabel={(file) => `Remove ${file.name}`} allowsMultiple acceptedFileTypes={['.pdf', 'image/*']} />

components.a11y: The button opens the picker. The drop area has its own focus stop where keyboard drag and drop and pasting a copied file work. Files left out by type or size raise a polite warning; each remove button names its file.

components.name: FilterChips
components.description: Quick filters above a list, with an optional count on each. Multiple mode toggles each chip on its own; single mode picks one. ChipCount is the count badge, also used inside tabs.

examples.code:
<FilterChips label="Status" selected={status} onChange={setStatus} clearLabel="Clear filters"
  chips={[{ id: 'open', label: 'Open', count: 42, countLabel: '42 issues' }]} />
<ChipCount value={1280} max={999} label="1280 issues" />

components.a11y: Multiple mode is a set of toggle buttons with aria-pressed; single mode is a radio group. An active chip gains a check mark and an accent border, so the state never rests on colour. Counts read as their label, such as "42 issues". The clear button returns focus to the chips once it goes away. Chips wrap on narrow screens.

components.name: FindingRow
components.description: Audit results: a score out of 100 with its grade, and findings with severity, rule and place that can be picked to send on together. Pick it for security, accessibility or SEO reports.

examples.code:
<ScoreBadge value={report.score} label={t('audit.score')} gradeLabels={{ good: t('grade.good'), fair: t('grade.fair'), poor: t('grade.poor') }} />
<List aria-label={t('audit.findings')} items={findings} selectionMode="multiple"
  selectedKeys={picked} onSelectionChange={setPicked} onAction={showDetails}>
  {(f) => <FindingRow id={f.id} severity={f.severity} severityLabel={t(`severity.${f.severity}`)}
    title={f.title} rule={f.rule} location={f.file ?? f.target} selectLabel={t('common.select')} />}
</List>

components.a11y: The score is a meter named by its label and reads the number with the grade word; the grade also shows as an icon and a word, so the ring colour is never the only clue, and it fills without motion under reduced motion. Severity is a word with a glyph that climbs with the level. Each finding has a checkbox named "Select" plus its title; Space selects, Enter shows the details. On a narrow row the place moves under the title and long selectors wrap.

components.name: FlashMessages
components.description: Messages the server left for the next page, such as "Saved" after a redirect or the errors of a form. Pick it for server-rendered results; use useToast for results of actions on the client.

examples.code:
<FlashMessages
  messages={[{ id: 'saved', tone: 'ok', title: 'Profile saved' }]}
  toneLabels={{ ok: 'Success', info: 'Information', warn: 'Warning', danger: 'Error' }}
  onDismiss={remove}
  dismissLabel="Close message"
  focusError
/>

components.a11y: Messages already in the page when it loads are not read by live regions, so each one is also written into a polite region after mount, and errors into an assertive one. focusError moves focus to the first error instead, which suits a form that came back from the server. Each message is read once and never closes on its own.

components.name: FocusTrap
components.description: Keeps Tab inside a panel of your own while it is open, then gives focus back. Modal, Popover and DropdownMenu already do this; pick FocusTrap for a custom drawer or a guided step.
components.a11y: Built on React Aria FocusScope. On mount focus goes to the first tabbable element, or stays on one inside that has autoFocus. Tab and Shift+Tab wrap at the ends, radio groups count as one stop, and focus returns to the opener on unmount. Give the panel a name and a way out, here Apply and Close, and close it on Escape where that fits.

components.name: FormActions
components.description: The button row at the end of a form, with the result of the last submit. Put the main button last.

examples.code:
<FormActions status={{ tone: 'ok', message: 'Saved' }}>
  <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</FormActions>

components.a11y: A failed save is an assertive alert; ok, info and warn messages are polite. Each message has an icon and words. Both regions stay mounted, so a message that appears later is announced. Buttons stack at full width on a narrow screen with the main one on top.

components.name: FormErrorSummary
components.description: The list of problems after a submit fails, placed at the top of the form. Use it with inline errors on each field, never instead of them.

examples.code:
<FormErrorSummary
  title="There are 2 problems with this form"
  errors={[{ fieldId: 'title', message: 'Enter a title' }]}
/>

components.a11y: It is an assertive alert and takes focus when it appears, so keyboard and screen reader users land on it after submitting. Each item is a link that moves focus to its field and scrolls it into view. The heading level is a prop, to fit the page outline. The demo keeps autoFocus off, so the gallery does not jump.

components.name: GatedAction
components.description: An action that is not available yet, with the reason and what unlocks it. Use it instead of a silently disabled button whenever the person can do something about it.

props.name: children
props.type: ReactNode | ((values: ButtonRenderProps & { defaultChildren: ReactNode | undefined }) => ReactNode)

examples.code:
<GatedAction isGated={!title} reason="Add a title to publish." onPress={publish}>
  Publish
</GatedAction>

components.a11y: Stays in the tab order with aria-disabled, so keyboard and screen reader users reach it and hear the reason, linked with aria-describedby. Presses and form submission are blocked. The reason is printed under the button, or shown as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus in tight spaces, and is never colour alone.

components.name: GitFileRow
components.description: One changed file with its kind as a letter, the name before the folder and actions for staging or discarding. Pick it for working tree and staged changes; put the rows in a List.

examples.code:
<List aria-label="Changes" items={files}>
  {(file) => (
    <GitFileRow id={file.path} path={file.path} kind={file.kind} kindLabel={t(`git.${file.kind}`)}
      onAction={() => openDiff(file)}
      actions={<IconButton label={t('git.stage', { path: file.path })} size="sm" onPress={() => stage(file)}><Icon name="action.add" aria-hidden /></IconButton>} />
  )}
</List>

components.a11y: The list is one tab stop: Up and Down move between files, typing jumps to a path, Enter runs onAction and Right reaches the buttons in the row. The kind is read as a word before the path; the letter on screen is hidden and also differs by shape (a deleted name is struck through). Hover actions stay in the page and show on focus, on touch screens and in forced colours.

components.name: GitGraph
components.description: The commit history with branch lines drawn in SVG, refs as badges, authors, dates and short hashes. Pick it for a history view where people pick a commit to inspect.

examples.code:
<GitGraph label={t('history.title')} commits={log} selectedHash={selected?.hash}
  onSelect={setSelected} mergeLabel={t('history.merge')} refKindLabels={{ tag: t('git.tag') }} />

<RefBadge kind="tag" kindLabel={t('git.tag')}>v0.4.0</RefBadge>

<GitGraph label={t('history.title')} commits={log} isLoading={loading}
  loadingLabel={t('history.loading')} error={failed && t('history.failed')} emptyState={t('history.empty')} />

components.a11y:
A single-select grid: arrow keys move, Enter or Space selects, typing jumps to a subject. Lines are decoration and hidden; merges are read as a word and drawn as a hollow dot. Ref kinds differ by glyph as well as colour, and their kind can be read before the name. The lines stretch with the row, so they stay joined at 200% text size, and turn to the text colour in forced colours.

Loading is a polite status, the error an assertive alert with an icon and words, and the empty text stays inside the named grid.

components.name: GlobalSearch
components.description: The search box of a top bar. The app filters on its side, often on a server, and passes grouped results; Enter with nothing highlighted submits the query for a full results page.

examples.code:
<GlobalSearch label="Search" value={q} onChange={setQ} onSubmit={openResults}
  shortcutKey="/" shortcutHint="/" emptyLabel="No results" resultsLabel={`${count} results`}>
  <SearchResultGroup id="issues" title="Issues">
    <SearchResultItem id="SK-12" textValue="Draft lost" title="Draft lost" href="/issues/SK-12" />
  </SearchResultGroup>
</GlobalSearch>

components.a11y: A combobox inside a search landmark with a hidden label. / focuses it from anywhere unless another field has focus, and aria-keyshortcuts tells screen readers. Up and Down move through results while focus stays in the field; Enter opens the highlighted result; Escape closes the list and then clears it. Groups are labelled by their titles. Result counts, loading and errors are read from a polite live region, and an error shows an icon with its text. The list keeps the field width and never runs off a narrow screen.

components.name: GlyphIcon
components.description: The complete Lucide set is plain glyph data under @skribly/ui/icons/lucide, one named export per icon. GlyphIcon draws it in the same three tones, and a bundler keeps only the icons you import. Prefer a registry name when one exists.

examples.code:
import { lucideAnchor } from '@skribly/ui/icons/lucide'

<GlyphIcon glyph={lucideAnchor} tone="duo" />

components.a11y: GlyphIcon follows the same rules as Icon. With no label it is aria-hidden: put a word beside it or name the control it sits in. With label it is role="img" with that name. The tones keep the contrast of Icon in each theme and in forced colours.

components.name: Hero
components.description: The welcome banner at the top of a home screen, with a greeting, one paragraph and the first actions. Use it once per page.

examples.code:
<Hero
  eyebrow="Monday, 9 November"
  title="Good morning. Your agents are ready."
  lead="One window for every coding agent."
  actions={<Button>Start an agent</Button>}
  aside={<AgentChip … />}
/>

components.a11y: A region named by its heading, which is an h1 unless level says otherwise. The art is hidden from screen readers and dropped on narrow containers so the text keeps the width. Actions and the aside wrap; the lead keeps a readable line length.

components.name: Highlight
components.description: Marks the part of a text that matched a search, by query or by the positions of a fuzzy match.

examples.code:
<GlobalSearch label="Search" value={q} onChange={setQ} onSubmit={openResults}
  shortcutKey="/" shortcutHint="/" emptyLabel="No results" resultsLabel={`${count} results`}>
  <SearchResultGroup id="issues" title="Issues">
    <SearchResultItem id="SK-12" textValue="Draft lost" title="Draft lost" href="/issues/SK-12" />
  </SearchResultGroup>
</GlobalSearch>

<Highlight text={title} query={query} />
<Highlight text={path} positions={match.positions} />

components.a11y:
A combobox inside a search landmark with a hidden label. / focuses it from anywhere unless another field has focus, and aria-keyshortcuts tells screen readers. Up and Down move through results while focus stays in the field; Enter opens the highlighted result; Escape closes the list and then clears it. Groups are labelled by their titles. Result counts, loading and errors are read from a polite live region, and an error shows an icon with its text. The list keeps the field width and never runs off a narrow screen.

Matches are mark elements with a heavier weight and an underline, so they never rely on colour, and both stay under forced colours. Accents and case are ignored, so "cafe" marks "Café".

components.name: Icon
components.description: mono follows the text colour, brand takes the accent, duo puts the accent stroke on the soft accent fill. Use brand or duo for the current item or a product mark, mono everywhere else.

examples.code:
<Icon name="nav.settings" />
<Icon name="status.ok" tone="brand" size="sm" />
<Icon name="cinema.seat" tone="duo" label="Seat" />
<Icon name="status.warning" size="sm" label="Warning" />
<Icon name="app.tracker" tone="duo" />

components.a11y: An icon with no label is aria-hidden: put a word beside it or name the control it sits in. With label it is role="img" with that name. The accent keeps 3:1 on every surface in each theme; in forced colours the fill drops and the stroke follows the system text colour.

components.name: IconButton
components.description: A square button with only an icon, for toolbars and dense rows where the icon is well known. Prefer a labelled Button when there is room.

props.name: children
props.type: ReactNode | ((values: ButtonRenderProps & { defaultChildren: ReactNode | undefined }) => ReactNode)

examples.code:
<IconButton label="Add item" onPress={add}>
  <Icon name="action.add" aria-hidden />
</IconButton>

components.a11y: label is the accessible name and also appears as a tooltip on hover and at once on keyboard focus, so sighted and voice control users know what to call it. Escape hides the tooltip. Each size is at least 24px square.

components.name: ImageEditor
components.description: Crop and focal point for one image, with optional rotate and flip. Use it in a dialog or a side panel when an image has to fit fixed shapes; the app does the actual image work through the callbacks.

examples.code:
<ImageEditor src={url} imageWidth={1920} imageHeight={1080} ratios={ratios}
  labels={labels} previews={[{ label: 'Square', ratio: 1 }]}
  onApplyCrop={crop} onSaveFocal={saveFocal} onRotate={rotate}
  status={result} isBusy={working} busyLabel="Working on the image" />

components.a11y: The crop frame is one tab stop, a slider that screen readers pass the arrow keys to: arrows move it, Shift and arrows resize it, and its position is read as words from cropValueText. Number boxes set the exact edges and size, and two sliders set the focal point, so nothing needs a pointer. Corners have 24px targets. Outcomes appear in words with a glyph: errors are announced at once and others politely, and they stay until replaced. The tools sit beside the preview when the editor is wide and under it otherwise; frame lines keep a contrasting edge on any image and use the system highlight in forced colours.

components.name: ImageField
components.description: A form field holding images from the library in order, such as a cover or a gallery. Pick it whenever a form saves image references; pair it with MediaPicker to add.

props.name: itemLabel
props.type: (file: MediaFile, index: number, count: number) => string

props.name: movedLabel
props.type: (file: MediaFile, index: number, count: number) => string

examples.code:
<ImageField label="Gallery" value={images} onChange={setImages}
  addLabel="Add images" onAdd={openPicker} name="gallery"
  itemLabel={(file, i, n) => `Image ${i + 1} of ${n}: ${file.name}`}

components.a11y: A fieldset named by its label. Each image is a grid row named with its position, and its buttons are reached with Tab. Moving announces the new position and keeps focus on a move button even at the ends; removing moves focus to the next image or the add button. Drag handles add keyboard and screen reader dragging. An error is linked to the add button with aria-describedby and aria-invalid and the list gets a dashed outline, so it shows without colour too. Use requiredLabel so "required" is read.

components.name: ImagePlaceholder

examples.code:

<ImagePlaceholder state="loading" label="Loading image" />
<ImagePlaceholder state="error" label="Image could not load"
