components.a11y: With a label it is an image with that name, and the description is linked to it; without one it is hidden. Loading is marked busy and its pulse stops under reduced motion. The error state shows a broken picture glyph and words, and becomes a group when it holds an action.

components.name: Inbox
components.description: A list of the notifications the app passes in, typed after the notification contract of core. Unread items come before read ones, and an agent waiting for a person comes before every other reason. Each item shows its reason, its time in the locale of the person and, when it has a link, its title as the link. Mark one or all as read; a new item is announced. The component fetches nothing.

examples.code:
<Inbox
  notifications={notifications}
  labels={labels}
  onOpen={(item) => markRead(item.id)}
  onMarkRead={markRead}
  onMarkAllRead={markAllRead}
  linkComponent={Link}
/>

<AppShell
  notifications={{
    label: 'Notifications, 2 new',
    title: 'Notifications',
    badge: 2,
    content: <Inbox notifications={items} labels={labels} variant="compact" limit={5} viewAllHref="/inbox" hideTitle />
  }}
/>

components.a11y: A region named by the title, with the items as a list. Unread items say so in words to a screen reader and show a dot and a bolder title, never colour alone; the tone has a glyph and, with labels.tones, a word. Tab reaches each link and each mark-read button, which has its own label and a tooltip. When a mark-read button goes, the focus moves to the title link of its item (or the item), and after mark all read to the title. New unread items are announced politely, the first render is not. Every target is at least 44px on touch.

components.name: InboxItem
components.description: One notification on its own, for a list an app lays out itself. isPriority gives the reason its warning badge.
components.a11y: Put it inside a ul or ol: it is a list item. Unread says so in words to a screen reader, with a dot and a bolder title, never colour alone. The title is a link only for an http, https or mailto url or a relative one; any other scheme leaves plain text. The mark-read button has its own label; when it goes, the focus moves to the title link or to the item.

components.name: InfoTip
components.description: A small round button beside a term that opens a short explanation. Pick it over Tooltip when the text matters, because it works by touch, by keyboard and at any zoom.

examples.code:
<InfoTip label="About the build time">
  The time from start to finish of the last run.
</InfoTip>

components.a11y: A real button with a name that says what it explains. Enter or a tap opens the text as a small dialog, Escape closes it and focus returns. The sm size is a 24px target, the WCAG 2.2 minimum; md is 32px.

components.name: Input
components.description: The bare text box, for building a field from React Aria parts or for a Field around it. Most forms want TextField, which includes the label.

examples.code: <Field label="Domain">{(control) => <Input {...control} />}</Field>

components.a11y: On its own it has no name: put it in a Field, a React Aria field, or give it an aria-label. Text is 16px under the sm breakpoint so iOS does not zoom in. The focus ring comes from the page defaults and stays visible in forced colours.

components.name: InputWithIcon
components.description: A text field with a leading icon and optional end text, such as a unit or a domain. The icon is a hint, never the label.

examples.code: <InputWithIcon label="Website" icon={<Icon name="nav.web" />} placeholder="example.com" />

components.a11y: The icon is hidden from screen readers and the end text is plain text after the input, so the label must say everything. Long values scroll inside the box.

components.name: IssueKey
components.description: The project key and number of an issue in the monospace face. Pick it wherever an issue is named, and pass href when the key should open the issue.

examples.code: <IssueKey href="/issues/SK-101">SK-101</IssueKey>

components.a11y: Plain text, or a React Aria link with a visible focus ring and a 24px tall target. translate="no" keeps page translators away from it. isClosed strikes it through, so say closed in words nearby as well, for example with a status badge.

components.name: IssueRow
components.description: One issue on one line, as on the dashboard. Pick it for short lists such as "Assigned to me"; use IssueTable for long lists people sort.

examples.code: {issues.map((issue) => ( ))}

components.a11y: The title is a link whose hit area covers the row, and the row draws its focus ring. isCurrent sets aria-current and adds an accent rule. Overdue dates change their glyph and read overdueLabel. In a narrow container the facts wrap under the title, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px or 400% zoom.

components.name: IssueStatusBadge
components.description: A status under the project’s own name, tinted by its category: not started, in progress, done or cancelled. Pick it for the status of an issue in lists, cards and headers.

examples.code: <IssueStatusBadge category="in_progress">{status.name}</IssueStatusBadge>

components.a11y: The name is plain text, so it is read as written. Each category has its own glyph shape (an empty ring, a dashed ring, a ticked ring, a struck ring), hidden from screen readers. Text and tint pairs come from the tokens in every theme, and a transparent border keeps the outline in forced colours. Long names truncate with the full name in the title.

components.name: IssueTable
components.description: The issue list of a project on the shared Table, with sorting, empty, loading and error states. Pick stack, the default, to turn rows into cards below 36rem, or scroll to keep the grid in its own scrolling box.

examples.code:
<IssueTable caption={t('issues.open')} issues={issues} headers={headers}
  labelsLabel={t('fields.labels')} unassignedLabel={t('issue.unassigned')}
  sort={sort} onSortChange={setSort} sortable={['key', 'priority']} />

components.a11y: A native table with a caption, column headers and the title as row header. Sortable headers are buttons and carry aria-sort. In the stacked layout each cell keeps its column name as a visible label and the table roles stay in place. Loading is a polite status, an error is an assertive alert with an icon.

components.name: IssueTypeBadge
components.description: The kind of an issue as a glyph and a word: bug, feature, task, improvement or epic. Pass icon for a kind the app defines itself.

examples.code: <IssueTypeBadge kind="bug" label={t('types.bug')} />

components.a11y: Each kind has its own glyph shape, hidden from screen readers; the word carries the meaning and stays for screen readers when compact hides it.

components.name: Kbd
components.description: Shows one key in running text or in a hint. Use KeyCombo for a combination.

examples.code:
Press <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> to close.
<Kbd label="Command">⌘</Kbd>

components.a11y: Renders a kbd element. A symbol key takes label, which screen readers say in place of the glyph, so "⌘" is read as "Command" rather than "place of interest sign".

components.name: KeyCombo
components.description: A keyboard shortcut: keys pressed together, a sequence, or several shortcuts that do the same thing. Use it in menus, tooltips and help pages.

examples.code:
<KeyCombo keys={['Ctrl', 'K']} separator="+" />
<KeyCombo keys={[['Ctrl', 'K'], ['/']]} separator="+" orLabel="or" />

components.a11y: A kbd element wraps one kbd per key, as HTML describes a combination. The separator is hidden from screen readers; the word between alternatives is read. Long combinations wrap, and the shortcut list in the demo stacks under 640px.

components.name: KeyValueList
components.description: Labelled facts about one thing, such as account or server details. The inline layout puts labels beside values when there is room and stacks them on a phone; columns fits more facts on wide screens.

examples.code:
<KeyValueList emptyValue="Not set" items={[
  { label: 'Email', value: user.email },
  { label: 'Plan', value: 'Team', hint: 'Renews on 1 December' }
]} />

components.a11y: A description list, so each value is read with its label. A missing value shows the emptyValue words rather than a blank. Long values such as email addresses wrap instead of overflowing, and the layout follows the width of its own box, so it reflows at 400% zoom.

components.name: LabelBadge
components.description: One label with the colour the project picked for it. Pass onRemove where labels are edited.

examples.code:
<LabelBadge color={label.color} onRemove={() => remove(label)} removeLabel={t('labels.remove', { name: label.name })}>
  {label.name}
</LabelBadge>

components.a11y: The colour only tints a dot hidden from screen readers; the text sits on the neutral surface, so any project colour keeps it readable. The remove button is 24px, named by removeLabel, with a visible focus ring. Long names truncate with the full name in the title.

components.name: LabelList
components.description: The labels of an issue as a named, wrapping list. Pick max where space is short; the rest fold behind a +N button.

examples.code:
<LabelList labels={issue.labels} label={t('fields.labels')} max={3}
  moreLabel={(n) => t('labels.more', { count: n })} lessLabel={t('labels.fewer')} />

components.a11y: A list named by label, so screen readers say how many labels there are. The +N button is named by moreLabel, says aria-expanded and controls the list; it keeps focus when the list opens and becomes the button that folds it back.

components.name: LanguageBanner
components.description: Tells the reader what happens to a translation: downloading, offline, failed or ready. It can repeat the message in a second language while the first is still missing.

examples.code:
<LanguageBanner state="offline" title="Offline" onDismiss={hide} dismissLabel="Dismiss"
  secondary={{ lang: 'pl', text: 'Brak internetu.' }}>
  The translation downloads once you are online.
</LanguageBanner>

components.a11y: A polite status region, so it never interrupts; keep it mounted and change its state so screen readers hear the update. Each state has its own icon and a title word as well as a colour. It never hides itself: it stays until the state changes or the reader dismisses it. The floating placement spans the width on narrow screens.

components.name: LanguagePicker
components.description: Finds a language in a long list by its own name, English name or code, with an optional field for any other code. Pick it for settings; use LanguageSwitch for two or three languages.

props.name: custom
props.type: { label: string buttonLabel: string placeholder?: string errorLabel: string isValid?: (code: string) => boolean }

examples.code:
<LanguagePicker label="Interface language" languages={languages} value={lang} onChange={setLang}
  emptyLabel="No language matches."
  custom={{ label: 'Other code', buttonLabel: 'Use code', errorLabel: 'Enter a code such as ga or pt-BR.' }} />

components.a11y: The search field filters the list as you type; Up and Down move through matches and Enter picks one while focus stays in the field. Names carry their own lang. A wrong custom code marks the field invalid, links the message with aria-describedby and moves focus back to it. The list scrolls inside its own box.

components.name: LanguageSwitch
components.description: A short row of language codes for a top bar. With onChange it switches in place; with href on each language it links to the same page in that language.

examples.code:
<LanguageSwitch label="Language" value={lang} onChange={setLang}
  languages={[{ code: 'pl', name: 'Polski' }, { code: 'en', name: 'English' }]} />

components.a11y: Buttons mode is a radio group; links mode is a nav with aria-current on the active language and hreflang on each link. Every option is read as its code and its own name, such as "PL Polski", tagged with its lang so the voice switches. The active code is underlined, not only coloured.

components.name: Lightbox
components.description: Opens a picture of a list in a full screen dialog. Zoom with the buttons, the wheel, a pinch or a double click, drag to pan while zoomed, move through a group with the arrows, a swipe or the thumbnails.

examples.code:
<Lightbox
  images={[{ src: '/a.webp', alt: 'A harbour' }, { src: '/b.webp', alt: 'A meadow' }]}
  index={index}
  onIndexChange={setIndex}
  isOpen={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  labels={labels}
/>

components.a11y: A modal dialog named by the dialog label: focus starts on Close, stays inside and returns to the picture that opened it. Escape and a click on the backdrop close it. Plus, minus and 0 zoom, the arrow keys pan while zoomed and move between pictures otherwise, Home and End jump to the ends. The position is announced politely. Controls keep their words as labels, and motion drops out with reduced motion.

components.name: LineChart
components.description: A trend over time for one or more measures on one axis. Pick it for daily or weekly series; add the previous period as a ghost line to compare, and annotations for releases or incidents.

examples.code:
<LineChart
  label="Visits, last 28 days"
  description="1,602 visits yesterday, 22 % more than the period before."
  keyboardHint="Use the arrow keys to read each day."
  categories={days.map(longDate)}
  axisLabels={days.map(shortDate)}
  series={[
    { id: 'visits', label: 'Visits', values },
    { id: 'previous', label: 'Previous 28 days', values: before, ghost: true }
  ]}
  annotations={[{ index: 14, label: 'Version 2.4 released' }]}
  annotationsLabel="Releases"
  table={{ trigger: 'Show as table', categoryHeader: 'Date', annotationHeader: 'Note' }}
/>

<LineChart {...props} isLoading loadingLabel="Loading visits" />
<LineChart {...props} error="The report could not be loaded. Try again in a minute." />
<BarChart {...props} data={[]} emptyState="No errors in this period." />

components.a11y:
A figure named by label and described by the summary. The plot is one tab stop: Left and Right (or Up and Down) move between points, Home and End jump to the ends, and each move is read through a polite live region with the date, every series and any note. Escape hides the tooltip, which also opens on hover and stays while the pointer is over the chart. Series differ by line pattern as well as colour, and the legend names them. The table lists every value. Gridlines, lines and labels use system colours in forced colours. The SVG redraws at the width of its box, so it reflows at 320 px and 400 % zoom.

Loading is a status that is read politely and marks the figure busy. An error is an alert with an icon and words, read at once. The empty state is plain text with an icon. None of them relies on colour, and the spinner stops under reduced motion.

components.name: LinkButton
components.description: Navigation that needs the weight of a button, such as "Read the guide" on an empty page. If it changes data rather than the page, use Button.

examples.code:
<LinkButton href="/docs">Read the guide</LinkButton>
<LinkButton href="https://status.example.com" target="_blank" newTabLabel="opens in a new tab">
  Status page
</LinkButton>

components.a11y: A real link: Enter follows it and the browser context menu works. A new-tab link shows an icon and appends newTabLabel for screen readers, and gets rel="noopener noreferrer".

components.name: LinkTabs
components.description: Looks like Tabs but each tab is a link to another page. Pick it for section navigation that changes the address.

examples.code:
<LinkTabs label="Project navigation" currentId="list" items={[
  { id: 'board', label: 'Board', href: '/p/board' },
  { id: 'list', label: 'List', href: '/p/list' }
]} />

components.a11y: A nav landmark with plain links, so Tab moves through them and the browser keeps history. The current page has aria-current="page" and an underline, never colour alone. Client routing works through RouterProvider.

components.name: List
components.description: An interactive list of records with an icon, title, description, trailing meta and row actions. Pick it over a table when each record reads as one line of text rather than as columns.

examples.code:
<List aria-label="Projects" items={projects} selectionMode="multiple">
  {(p) => (
    <ListItem id={p.id} title={p.name} description={p.description}
      meta={<Badge tone="ok">Live</Badge>}
      actions={<IconButton label={`Deploy ${p.name}`} size="sm"><Icon name="ops.deploy" aria-hidden="true" /></IconButton>} />
  )}
</List>

<List aria-label="Projects" items={items} isLoading={loading} loadingLabel="Loading projects"
  error={failed ? 'Could not load projects.' : undefined} emptyState="No projects yet.">
  {(p) => <ListItem id={p.id} title={p.name} />}
</List>

components.a11y:
One tab stop; Up and Down move between items, Home and End jump, typing finds an item, Space selects and Enter runs onAction. Right arrow reaches the buttons inside an item. Selected items have a checkbox named after the item, a tint and a leading rule, and the system highlight in forced colours. Titles wrap at large zoom unless truncate is set.

Each item gets a drag handle with a 24px target. From the keyboard, focus the handle and press Enter to pick the item up, move with the arrow keys and press Enter to drop; React Aria announces each step, and Escape cancels.

Loading is a polite status, an error an assertive alert with an icon and words, and the empty state stays inside the named list.

components.name: LiveRegion
components.description: LiveRegion reads changes to its content aloud, such as a result count after filtering. useAnnounce speaks a one-off message without showing it, such as "Draft saved" after a shortcut.

examples.code:
<LiveRegion>{count} results</LiveRegion>

const announce = useAnnounce()
announce('Draft saved')
announce('Could not reach the server', 'assertive')

components.a11y: Polite messages wait for the screen reader to finish; assertive ones interrupt and are only for errors that block the reader. Render a LiveRegion empty from the start, because a region that appears with its text is often not read. Announcements stay readable while a modal dialog is open, and the same message twice is read twice.

components.name: LocalePicker
components.description: Adds a language to a site by search, not by typing a code. The list is every language Intl names, in the panel language and in the language itself, and a typed BCP 47 tag such as pt-BR, sr-Latn or yue is offered in its canonical spelling. Pick it for the languages of content; use LanguagePicker for the language of the interface.

examples.code:
<LocalePicker label={t('languages.add')} displayLocale={panelLocale} emptyLabel={t('languages.none')}
  disabledLocales={site.locales} disabledLabel={t('languages.added')} rtlLabel={t('languages.rtl')}
  moreLabel={(hidden) => t('languages.more', { hidden })} onChange={(tag, option) => addLocale(tag, option.direction)} />

components.a11y: The search field filters the list as you type; Up and Down move through the matches and Enter picks one while focus stays in the field. The name in the language itself carries its lang and dir. A right-to-left language and a language already added say so in words, never colour alone, and an added one is disabled. The list scrolls inside its own box and shows at most limit matches, with a line that says how many more there are.

components.name: LoginForm
components.description: Email and password sign in with remember me, a password reset link and a show password button. Checks run in the browser first; the server adds field errors and a notice. Try any password, then "skribly".

examples.code:
<LoginForm
  labels={labels}
  forgotHref="/forgot-password"
  onSubmit={async (values) => {
    const result = await signIn(values)
    if (!result.ok) setNotice({ tone: 'danger', title: 'Sign in failed', toneLabel: 'Error' })
  }}
  notice={notice}
/>

components.a11y: A failed submit puts focus on an error summary whose links move focus to each field. Every field error is tied to its input with aria-describedby and aria-invalid and clears as soon as the field is fixed. A failed sign in is read at once from an assertive region; other notices wait their turn. The submit button stays focused while pending and its spinner is named. Caps Lock is reported politely, and the show password button keeps one name with a pressed state.

components.name: Logo
components.description: The Skribly mark, plain or with the glyph and colour of a product. Every product has one, listed in marks; products differ by glyph and colour and by nothing else. Use tone="nav" on the dark sidebar.

examples.code:
<Logo kind="agent" size={32} label="Skribly Agent" />
<Logo kind="hub" size={48} label="Skribly Hub" />
<Logo kind="tracker" tone="nav" />

components.a11y: Decoration unless label is set, then an image with that name. Leave label out when the name is written next to it. The size is in rem, so it grows with the reader’s text size. The product colour is never the only sign: the glyph and the written name tell the products apart.

components.name: MainContent
components.description: The scrolling main column, the target of the skip link. Pick width wide for boards and tables, full for editors.

examples.code:
<MainContent width="wide">
  <PageHeader title="Board" />
  …
</MainContent>

components.a11y: The main landmark, with tabindex -1 so the skip link can move focus into it, and a tab stop while its content overflows, so the keyboard can scroll text with nothing focusable in it; its ring shows only for keyboard focus. Padding grows with the layout, and the scrollbar gutter is kept stable so content does not jump.

components.name: Markdown
components.description: Renders Markdown from a user, a tracker or an agent as safe HTML. It runs on the server too, with no DOM, so pick it for any stored Markdown text.

examples.code: <Markdown text={issue.description} headingOffset={2} tableLabel="Table" />

components.a11y: Raw HTML is shown as text and only http, https, mailto, tel and relative links are kept. headingOffset keeps the heading outline under the page heading. Task items are read-only checkboxes named by their text. Tables and code blocks scroll in their own box, which takes keyboard focus.

components.name: MarkdownField
components.description: A text area for Markdown with a preview tab, for descriptions and comments. Pick it when the text will be shown rendered; use a plain TextField for short values.

examples.code:
<MarkdownField
  label="Description"
  writeLabel="Write"
  previewLabel="Preview"
  emptyPreview="Nothing to preview yet."
  value={text}
  onChange={setText}
  isInvalid={!text}
  errorMessage="Enter a description."
/>

components.a11y: The label names the text area and the tab list. Arrow keys move between Write and Preview, and the text stays when you switch. The description and the error are linked with aria-describedby, and aria-invalid is set. The open tab is marked by shape, not only colour, and stays visible in forced colours.

components.name: MediaGrid
components.description: The files of a folder as tiles or as a list, with selection for bulk actions, an action per file, drag to reorder and files dropped from the desktop. Pick it for any library view; use MediaTile alone for one file outside a list.

props.name: onMove
props.type: (keys: Key[], target: { key: Key; position: 'before' | 'after' }) => void

examples.code:
<MediaGrid aria-label="Files in Holidays" items={files} view="grid"
  selectionMode="multiple" selectedKeys={selected} onSelectionChange={setSelected}
  selectLabel="Select" onAction={openEditor}
  renderActions={(file) => <IconButton label={`Edit ${file.name}`} …/>}
  onMove={reorder} dragLabel={(file) => `Drag ${file.name}`}
  isLoading={loading} loadingLabel="Loading files"
  emptyState={<EmptyState title="This folder is empty" />} />

components.a11y: A React Aria grid with one tab stop. Arrow keys move between tiles in both directions, typing a file name jumps to it, Space or the checkbox selects, Enter runs the action and Tab reaches the buttons inside the focused tile. Checkboxes are read as "Select" plus the file name. Dragging works with the pointer, with Enter on the drag handle and the arrow keys, and with screen readers. Loading is a busy status with skeleton tiles, the empty state says why it is empty, notices such as a missing alt text carry a word and a glyph, and selected tiles get a border as well as a tint. Tiles reflow from one column at 320px.

components.name: MediaPicker
components.description: A dialog for choosing one or more files from the library, with search, folders and upload. Use it behind an ImageField or any "choose an image" button.

examples.code:
<MediaPicker trigger={<Button>Open the library</Button>} title="Media library"
  closeLabel="Close" cancelLabel="Cancel" gridLabel="Images" selectLabel="Select"
  chooseLabel={(n) => `Choose ${n}`} countLabel={(n) => `${n} chosen`}
  items={files} onChoose={setChosen}
  search={{ label: 'Search images', value: query, onChange: setQuery }}
  folders={{ label: 'Folder', chips, selected: folder, onChange: setFolder }} />

components.a11y: A modal dialog named by its title: focus moves in and is held there, Escape and the close button leave it, and focus returns to the trigger. On a phone it rises from the bottom as a sheet, with the actions in a footer that never scrolls away. Choices survive a search or a folder change, the count is announced, and the choose button stays disabled until something is chosen. In single mode a click or Enter on a tile chooses it at once, and its checkbox only selects it. A load error is an assertive alert with a way to retry.

components.name: MediaTile
components.description: One file: a thumbnail or the glyph of its kind, the name, the size and a notice. Use it alone in a sidebar or a detail view; MediaGrid uses it for every tile.

examples.code:
<MediaTile file={{ id: 1, name: 'harbour.webp', kind: 'image', kindLabel: 'Image',
  src, alt: 'Hills over a calm bay', details: '182 KB · 1920×1080',
  notice: { tone: 'warn', label: 'No alt text' } }}
  brokenLabel="Preview not available"
  actions={<Button size="sm" variant="outline">Edit</Button>} />

components.a11y: The thumbnail uses the file alt text, or none for decorative images, so the name is not read twice. A thumbnail that fails to load becomes a named placeholder in the danger tone. Long names wrap onto two lines and stay whole for screen readers. Buttons stay visible instead of appearing on hover, and the selected state is a border and a checked box, not a colour.

components.name: MenuCheckItem
components.description: A menu row that can be checked, for view settings such as visible columns. It needs a selectionMode on the menu or on its MenuLabel group.

examples.code:
<DropdownMenu trigger={<Button>Columns</Button>} selectionMode="multiple" selectedKeys={keys} onSelectionChange={setKeys}>
  <MenuCheckItem id="title">Title</MenuCheckItem>
  <MenuCheckItem id="owner">Owner</MenuCheckItem>
</DropdownMenu>

components.a11y: A multiple selection gives menuitemcheckbox rows, a single one menuitemradio, each with aria-checked. Checked rows show a check or a dot and bolder text, never colour alone.

components.name: MenuItem
components.description: A list of actions behind a button. MenuItem rows take an icon, a description, a shortcut and a danger tone; pick a menu for commands, not for choosing a form value.

examples.code:
<DropdownMenu trigger={<IconButton label="Help"><Icon name="status.help" /></IconButton>} onAction={run}>
  <MenuItem id="guide" icon={<Icon name="nav.help" />}>Start the guide</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem id="delete" tone="danger">Delete</MenuItem>
</DropdownMenu>

components.a11y: Enter, Space or Arrow Down opens it on the first row, Arrow Up on the last. Arrows move, typing jumps to a row, Enter runs it and Escape closes. The menu is named by its trigger, each row by all of its text, label first, so a description is read with it, and icons are hidden. Rows are at least 32px tall.

components.name: MenuLabel
components.description: A labelled group of menu rows with a dividing line before it. A group can hold its own selection, such as one theme mode next to plain actions.

examples.code:
<MenuLabel label="Theme mode" selectionMode="single" selectedKeys={mode} onSelectionChange={setMode}>
  <MenuCheckItem id="light">Light</MenuCheckItem>
  <MenuCheckItem id="dark">Dark</MenuCheckItem>
</MenuLabel>

components.a11y: The group has role="group" and is named by its visible label, so a screen reader says "Theme mode, group" when entering it.

components.name: MessageBubble
components.description: One message: your own on the end side in the accent colour, others on the start side. Shows author, time, a typing mark and delivery state with retry.

examples.code:
<MessageBubble from="me" author="You" hideAuthor time="2026-11-08T14:02" timeLabel="14:02" status={{ tone: 'danger', label: 'Not sent' }} onRetry={retry} retryLabel="Try again">
  Ship it?
</MessageBubble>

components.a11y: Each message is an article named by its author and time, even when the author is hidden on screen. A failed send is read out at once with its word; other states are shown with an icon and a word. The typing mark is read as its required pendingLabel, its dots stop pulsing under reduced motion and stay visible in Windows high contrast. Action buttons stay visible for touch and keyboard.

components.name: MessageThread
components.description: The scrolling log of a chat. It keeps the newest message in view, shows a jump button when you scroll up, and shows who is writing. Pick it for any back-and-forth with a person or an agent.

examples.code:
<MessageThread label="Chat with Claude Code" jumpLabel="Jump to the newest message" isBusy={busy} busyLabel="Claude Code is writing">
  {messages.map((m) => <MessageBubble key={m.id} from={m.from} author={m.author}>{m.text}</MessageBubble>)}
</MessageThread>

components.a11y: A named log in the tab order, so arrow keys scroll it. While a reply streams, aria-busy holds the announcement until the reply is complete. The writing state is a polite status. The jump button moves focus back to the log.

components.name: Meter
components.description: A level within a known range, such as storage used or a score. Pick ProgressBar for work that moves towards done.

examples.code: <Meter label="Disk space" value={92} tone="danger" status="Almost full" valueLabel="92 of 100 GB" />

components.a11y: A meter role named by its label, with the value and valueLabel read as text. A warning or danger tone takes a status word with its icon, linked to the meter as its description. The value text is also on screen, so the bar is never the only sign. The fill turns Highlight in forced colours.

components.name: MetricTile
components.description: One key figure with its change and recent trend, for a row of tiles at the top of a report. Pick StatCard of the surfaces group when the tile links to a full view.

examples.code:
<MetricTile
  label="Visits"
  value="38,412"
  delta={<Delta value={0.22} directionLabels={directions} comparison="vs previous 28 days" />}
  sparkline={last28}
  sparklineLabel="Visits, last 28 days: rising"
  hint="Last 28 days"
/>

components.a11y: Plain text in reading order: label, value, change, trend, hint. The sparkline is one image named by sparklineLabel. Loading marks the tile busy and reads loadingLabel; an error shows an icon and words. The value shrinks in a narrow tile and long text wraps, so four tiles fit two by two on a phone.

components.name: Modal
components.description: A dialog that blocks the page until it is closed. Pick it for a short task, such as a form or a choice, that must finish before going on; the body scrolls and the actions stay in view.

examples.code:
<Modal
  trigger={<Button>Rename project</Button>}
  title="Rename project"
  closeLabel="Close"
  footer={<><Button variant="outline" slot="close">Cancel</Button><Button onPress={save}>Save</Button></>}
>
  <TextField label="Project name" />
</Modal>

components.a11y: Focus moves into the dialog, Tab stays inside it, Escape and the close button close it, and focus goes back to the trigger. The title names the dialog and the description describes it. The rest of the page is hidden from screen readers while it is open. Built to WCAG 2.2 AA.

components.name: MoneyInput
components.description: An amount of money, typed and shown in the currency format of the locale with the decimals that currency has. The value is in major units, or in whole minor units with minorUnits, and null when empty. An optional currency choice sits beside the amount.

examples.code: <MoneyInput label="Amount" currency="PLN" value={amount} onChange={setAmount} />

components.a11y: The amount is a spin button text field: the arrow keys step it, and the formatted value with its currency is read out. Without allowNegative the minus sign cannot be typed. The currency choice is a separate labelled select, and each currency is named in the locale, not only by its code.

components.name: MultiSelect
components.description: Several choices from a known list, such as labels or channels. For free text that becomes tags, use ChipInput.

examples.code:
<MultiSelect label="Labels" items={labels}
  formatSelection={(names) => names.length > 2 ? `${names.length} labels` : names.join(', ')} />

components.a11y: The list stays open while choosing; Space or Enter toggles an option and Escape closes. Each row shows a check box glyph as well as the selected state React Aria announces. The trigger text is cut with an ellipsis, so give formatSelection a count for long choices.

components.name: NavGroup
components.description: A titled set of NavItems in a compact Sidebar, shown as a plain heading. The option to collapse exists only for a short compact list; never use it for nested navigation, which is the job of SidebarRail, where deeper pages open to the side.

examples.code:
<NavGroup label="Boards" currentLabel="contains the open page" isCollapsible={false}>
  <NavItem href="/boards/web">Website relaunch</NavItem>
</NavGroup>

components.a11y: The heading is plain text and never a toggle, and currentLabel is read after its name when the open page is inside. If you do turn on collapsing for a short compact list, the heading becomes a button with aria-expanded, toggled by Enter or Space, and it opens by itself when the open page moves into it. Nested navigation never collapses: use SidebarRail.

components.name: NavItem
components.description: One link of the sidebar with an icon and an optional NavKey or count at the end. NavKey shows a short code, such as a project key.

examples.code: <NavItem href="/boards/web" icon={<Icon name="nav.dashboard" tone="duo" />} end={<NavKey>WEB</NavKey>}>Website relaunch</NavItem>

components.a11y: The open page is marked four ways: a rule on the start edge, a lighter slab, a heavier label and an accent glyph, and aria-current="page" for screen readers; in forced colours the rule uses the Highlight colour and the label is underlined. The target is at least 36px tall. Choosing a link closes the sidebar sheet.

components.name: NavKey
components.description: One link of the sidebar with an icon and an optional NavKey or count at the end. NavKey shows a short code, such as a project key.

examples.code: <NavItem href="/boards/web" icon={<Icon name="nav.dashboard" tone="duo" />} end={<NavKey>WEB</NavKey>}>Website relaunch</NavItem>

components.a11y: The open page is marked four ways: a rule on the start edge, a lighter slab, a heavier label and an accent glyph, and aria-current="page" for screen readers; in forced colours the rule uses the Highlight colour and the label is underlined. The target is at least 36px tall. Choosing a link closes the sidebar sheet.

components.name: NudgeButtons
components.description: One step up and one step down: the keyboard and single-pointer way to reorder a list, next to or in place of dragging (WCAG 2.5.7). Horizontal lists use left and right.

examples.code:
<NudgeButtons
  label={`Reorder ${item}`}
  previousLabel={`Move ${item} up`}
  nextLabel={`Move ${item} down`}
  isFirst={index === 0}
  isLast={index === items.length - 1}
  onMove={(direction) => move(index, direction)}
/>

components.a11y: Each button names the item. The ends of the list are disabled so the position is visible without trying. Focus follows the moved item, and moves to the partner button when the pressed one reaches an end. The list announces the new position through its own polite live region, as the demo does.

components.name: OnboardingStep
components.description: A first-run card with what to set up, how far along the reader is and a button per step. Feed isDone from real data, so a step is done when the thing exists, not when it was ticked.

examples.code:
<OnboardingSteps title="First steps" doneLabel="done" todoLabel="to do"
  progressLabel={(done, total) => `${done} of ${total} done`}
  completeMessage="All set">
  <OnboardingStep title="Add a project" isDone={projects.length > 0} actionLabel="Add project" onAction={add} />
</OnboardingSteps>

components.a11y: A region named by its title with a progress bar whose value is read in words. Each row says "done" or "to do" after its title, and a done row also shows a check and a strike-through. Every action is named with its row, such as "Connect, Connect a task tracker". Errors carry an icon and a word; the complete message is announced politely.

components.description: A first-run card with what to set up, how far along the reader is and a button per step. Feed isDone from real data, so a step is done when the thing exists, not when it was ticked.

  completeMessage="All set">

</OnboardingSteps>

components.a11y: A region named by its title with a progress bar whose value is read in words. Each row says "done" or "to do" after its title, and a done row also shows a check and a strike-through. Every action is named with its row, such as "Connect, Connect a task tracker". Errors carry an icon and a word; the complete message is announced politely.

components.name: OptionCard
components.description: Selectable tiles with a preview, for choices people judge by eye: themes, fonts, animations. One choice makes a radio group, selectionMode="multiple" a checkbox group.

examples.code:
<OptionCardGroup label="Theme" value={theme} onChange={setTheme}>
  <OptionCard value="light" label="Light" preview={<ThemeSwatch />} selectedLabel="Selected" />
  <OptionCard value="dark" label="Dark" preview={<ThemeSwatch />} selectedLabel="Selected" />
</OptionCardGroup>

components.a11y: Built on React Aria radio and checkbox groups: Tab enters the group, arrow keys move, Space selects, and disabled tiles are skipped. The label names the group and each tile is named by its label and described by its description; previews are hidden. The chosen tile gets a check mark, an accent border and the selectedLabel word, and Highlight in Windows high contrast. Errors show under the grid and are linked to the group.

components.name: OptionCardGroup
components.description: Selectable tiles with a preview, for choices people judge by eye: themes, fonts, animations. One choice makes a radio group, selectionMode="multiple" a checkbox group.

examples.code:
<OptionCardGroup label="Theme" value={theme} onChange={setTheme}>
  <OptionCard value="light" label="Light" preview={<ThemeSwatch />} selectedLabel="Selected" />
  <OptionCard value="dark" label="Dark" preview={<ThemeSwatch />} selectedLabel="Selected" />
</OptionCardGroup>

components.a11y: Built on React Aria radio and checkbox groups: Tab enters the group, arrow keys move, Space selects, and disabled tiles are skipped. The label names the group and each tile is named by its label and described by its description; previews are hidden. The chosen tile gets a check mark, an accent border and the selectedLabel word, and Highlight in Windows high contrast. Errors show under the grid and are linked to the group.

components.name: OutputBox
components.description: Program output such as an install or build log, with an optional outcome. Pick it for text a tool printed; pick CodeBlock for source code.

examples.code:
<OutputBox
  label="Install output"
  title="npm install"
  text={output}
  isRunning={running}
  runningLabel="Running"
  status={{ tone: 'ok', label: 'Done' }}
/>

components.a11y: The outcome has a colour, an icon and a word. The header is a polite status region, so the change from running to done is read once, not every line. The output keeps the newest line in view unless you scrolled up, and the box is in the tab order for keyboard scrolling.

components.name: PageHeader
components.description: The heading row of a screen: an eyebrow, the title, a description and actions. Use one per screen, at the top of MainContent.

examples.code: <PageHeader eyebrow="Projects" title="Website relaunch" description="Issues grouped by status." actions={<Button>New issue</Button>} />

components.a11y: The eyebrow and the title form an hgroup, and the title is a level 1 heading unless level says otherwise. Long titles wrap, and the actions move under the title when space runs out.

components.name: Pagination
components.description: Moves through a long list split into pages. Pass getHref for real links that work without JavaScript, or onChange for buttons inside an app. A site splits a long list into static pages with the site kit: Pagination.astro has the same look.

examples.code:
<Pagination label="Pages" page={page} pageCount={24} onChange={setPage}
  previousLabel="Previous" nextLabel="Next" firstLabel="First page" lastLabel="Last page"
  pageLabel={(n) => `Page ${n}`} statusLabel={(n, total) => `Page ${n} of ${total}`} />

components.a11y: A named nav landmark. Every page control has a name such as "Page 3", the current one has aria-current="page" and a filled style, and Previous and Next are disabled at the ends. When its box is narrow the page numbers give way to a "Page 6 of 24" status with First and Last beside it, and Previous and Next keep only their arrows, still named for screen readers. Every target grows to 44 pixels on a touch screen.

components.name: Pane
components.description: A scrolling panel of a split layout with a sticky header. Use the side variant for a list beside the work and sunken for a panel under it.

examples.code:
<Pane variant="side">
  <PaneHeader title="Files" icon={<Icon name="folder.closed" />} actions={<IconButton label="Refresh">…</IconButton>} />
  …
</Pane>

components.a11y: The PaneHeader heading names the pane, so it becomes a region. While its content overflows the pane is a Tab stop, so the keyboard can scroll it; its ring is drawn inside so the edge never clips it.

components.name: PaneHeader
components.description: A scrolling panel of a split layout with a sticky header. Use the side variant for a list beside the work and sunken for a panel under it.

examples.code:
<Pane variant="side">
  <PaneHeader title="Files" icon={<Icon name="folder.closed" />} actions={<IconButton label="Refresh">…</IconButton>} />
  …
</Pane>

components.a11y: The PaneHeader heading names the pane, so it becomes a region. While its content overflows the pane is a Tab stop, so the keyboard can scroll it; its ring is drawn inside so the edge never clips it.

components.name: PasswordResetForm
components.description: The first step of a reset: the reader asks for a link by email. Say that a link is on its way whether or not the address has an account.

examples.code: <PasswordResetForm step="request" labels={labels} backHref="/login" onSubmit={sendLink} notice={notice} />

<PasswordResetForm
  step="reset"
  labels={labels}
  minLength={12}
  defaultEmail={email}
  hiddenFields={{ token }}
  onSubmit={savePassword}
/>

components.a11y:
The same summary, field errors and live notices as LoginForm. The back link is underlined and has a 24px target. The address field uses autocomplete="email".

The password rules sit under the field as its description, so they are read before typing. Both fields use autocomplete="new-password", so password managers suggest a strong one. A warning that the link expires is a tone, an icon and a word.

components.name: Pattern
components.description: The six brand patterns, drawn from the blocks and dots of the mark: grid, dots (a dotted margin), mosaic, ruled, hero and empty. The first five sit behind content in the product colour; empty is a small picture for an empty state. Load patterns.css, which plain.css and styles.css bring.

examples.code: Board

components.a11y: Decoration only: the pattern is a pseudo-element, so it is never read and never takes a click, and without children the element is hidden from assistive technology. The tint keeps body text at 4.5:1 (7:1 in high contrast) on every page surface and the weight under 3 percent. Nothing moves, and Windows high contrast and print leave the pattern out.

components.name: PipelineStepNode
components.description: One step of a pipeline of agents: its role, agent, prompt and status. Pick it for the nodes of a pipeline graph or a list of steps; steps of one stage run in parallel.

examples.code:
<PipelineStepNode
  title="Reviewer"
  meta="Claude Code · reads only"
  prompt={step.prompt}
  status="running"
  statusLabel={t('status.running')}
  onSelect={() => show(step.id)}
  isSelected={shown === step.id}
  expandLabel={t('showAll')}
  collapseLabel={t('showLess')}
/>

components.a11y: An article with the role as a heading. Each status has its own icon shape and its word, so the frame colour is never the only sign; the running spinner slows under reduced motion. With onSelect the title is a toggle button that reports whether the step is shown. A long prompt is cut to three lines with a button that reports whether it is expanded. On a narrow screen the stages stack.

components.name: PluginRow
components.description: An installed plugin or server with a switch that takes effect at once, its id, version, scope and description. The second list shows the loading state.

examples.code:
<List aria-label={t('plugins.installed')} items={plugins} emptyState={t('plugins.none')}>
  {(p) => <PluginRow id={p.id} title={p.title} identifier={p.id} version={p.version} versionLabel={t('common.version')}
    badges={<Badge size="sm">{t(`scope.${p.scope}`)}</Badge>} description={p.description}
    isEnabled={p.enabled} onEnabledChange={(on) => toggle(p, on)} switchLabel={t('plugins.enable', { name: p.title })}
    isBusy={busy === p.id} busyLabel={t('plugins.updating', { name: p.title })} />}
</List>

components.a11y: The switch is named after the plugin and says on or off; it waits while a change runs, with a named spinner beside it. The result is confirmed with a polite message that stays until closed. Right arrow reaches the switch and buttons; the description is clamped on screen only and read whole.

components.name: Popover
components.description: A small panel attached to a button, for extra controls or details that do not need the whole screen. Prefer it to a Modal when the page should stay in view.

examples.code:
<Popover trigger={<Button>Share</Button>} title="Share this page">
  {(close) => <Button onPress={close}>Copy link</Button>}
</Popover>

components.a11y: The trigger reports aria-expanded. The panel is a dialog named by its title, or by label when it has none. Focus moves in and returns to the trigger on Escape or a click outside. It never grows wider than the screen.

components.name: PresetFields
components.description: The fields of one image preset: name, size, fit, format, quality, weight limit and rules. Use it in the form that creates or edits a preset.

examples.code:
<PresetFields value={preset} onChange={setPreset} labels={labels}
  fitOptions={fits} formatOptions={formats}
  errors={{ name: 'Give the preset a name.' }}
  notes={{ keepTransparency: { tone: 'warn', message: 'JPEG has no transparency.' } }} />

components.a11y: Every field has a visible label, and optional ones say so in words. Number boxes step with the arrow keys and read the value in the reader locale; units are shown and named in the labels. Errors are linked with aria-describedby and set aria-invalid; notes that do not block, such as the JPEG warning, carry a glyph and words. The grid goes from one column on a phone to four on a wide screen.

components.name: PreviewFrame
components.description: The live preview of a page beside its editor: a phone, tablet or desktop width drawn at its real size and scaled, zoom, rotate, the address, reload and open in a new tab. usePreviewBridge sends the draft to the page and hears which block was clicked. For the preview of a development server use BrowserBar and DeviceFrame. The address must be http, https or a relative path: javascript:, data: and other schemes show the refused message instead of the frame and the open link. A page on the origin of the editor, like this demo, loses allow-same-origin when the sandbox also allows scripts, so it cannot reach the editor or lift its sandbox; serve the preview from its own origin when it needs the bridge.
components.a11y: The tools are a named group: the device and zoom choices are radio groups whose options have names even when only icons show, rotate is a toggle button, the address is a read-only field that can be selected and copied, and open says it opens a new tab. The frame has a title, and the box around it is a region named by that title in the tab order, so the keyboard can scroll a device wider or taller than the box. While the page loads the box is busy and shows a named spinner. The bridge posts only to the frame origin when it is allowed and accepts only typed messages from the frame window and an allowed origin, never from an opaque one, and runs nothing it receives.

components.name: PriorityBadge
components.description: The priority of an issue as an arrow glyph and a word. Pick compact on cards, where only the glyph shows.

examples.code: <PriorityBadge level="high" label={t('priority.high')} fieldLabel={t('fields.priority')} compact />

components.a11y: Arrows climb with the level, so the order reads without colour. The word is always in the page: compact hides it from sight only, and fieldLabel is read before it, so a card says "Priority High". The glyph is hidden from screen readers.

components.name: ProgressBar
components.description: Progress of a task towards done, such as an upload or an import. Leave out value while the length is unknown.

examples.code: <ProgressBar label="Uploading report.pdf" value={45} description="2 MB of 4.4 MB" />

components.a11y: A progressbar role named by its label; description is linked as its description. Without a value it is indeterminate and has no aria-valuenow. A finished or failed state takes a status word with its icon. The indeterminate pulse stops under reduced motion. Announce the end of a long task with a toast.

components.name: Prose
components.description: Gives plain HTML the reading styles of Skribly. Pick it for long text written in JSX or HTML from your own source; use Markdown for Markdown.

examples.code:
Getting started

Install the app and add a project.

components.a11y: Styles only, so the HTML inside keeps its own meaning. Links are underlined, not told by colour alone. Long words and addresses wrap, so the text reflows at 400% zoom.

components.name: PullRequestCard
components.description: The pull request of the current branch, or the next step towards one: install the tool, sign in, then create. Each state has its own icon, a colour and a word. Walk through the steps in the demo.

examples.code:
<PullRequestCard state="open" stateLabel={t('pr.open')} number="#128"
  title={pr.title} description={`${branch} → ${base}`} href={pr.url} />

<PullRequestCard state="none" stateLabel={t('pr.none')} title={t('pr.pushed', { base })}
  action={<Button size="sm" onPress={create} isPending={creating}>{t('pr.create')}</Button>} />

components.a11y: The state is a word in a badge, never only the icon colour. The title is a link when href is set and wraps instead of being cut. While an action runs the card sets aria-busy and its button says it is pending. Pass openInNewTab only when the text says the link opens a new tab.

components.name: QuickOpen
components.description: Go to a file by a few letters of its name, ranked like a code editor. ":120" after the name opens the file at that line.

examples.code:
<QuickOpen isOpen={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} shortcut paths={paths} recent={recent}
  onOpen={(path, { line }) => openFile(path, line)}
  label="Go to file" searchLabel="File name" listLabel="Files" closeLabel="Close" emptyLabel="No file matches." />

components.a11y: A modal dialog with a search field and a list of files. Each file is named by its file name, then its folder, plus "recently opened" where it applies. Matched letters are marked by weight and underline as well as colour. Up and Down move, Enter opens, Escape closes. The number of matches is read from a polite live region.

components.name: Radio
components.description: One choice from two to six options that should all be visible. For more, use Select.

examples.code:
<RadioGroup label="Visibility" defaultValue="team">
  <Radio value="private">Only me</Radio>

components.name: RefBadge

components.name: SessionClock
components.description: Small read-only figures for a session: time, context used and subagents. Pick ToolbarStat for any other figure; the three others format their value and switch tone on their own.

examples.code:

<ToolbarStat label={t('toolCalls')} value="14" icon={<Wrench />} />

components.name: SessionPeek
components.description: A glance at a session’s screen next to its row, without opening it. Pick it for lists of sessions where switching costs a context change.

examples.code:

  <Button>{name}</Button>
</SessionPeek>

components.a11y: Built on React Aria’s PreviewTrigger: it opens after a short hover, on keyboard focus or on a long press, the pointer can move onto it without it closing, and Escape closes it. Tab from the trigger moves into the screen, a named group a screen reader can read line by line. It never takes the place of opening the session, which the trigger itself does.

components.name: SessionStateChip
components.description: The state of one agent session: starting, working, waiting for you, done, ready or exited. Pick it wherever a session is listed; make it a button when the app can explain how the state was detected.

examples.code:

<SessionStateChip state="done" label={t('state.done')} onPress={explain} actionLabel={t('state.why')} />

components.a11y: The word is always in the page; hideLabel keeps it for screen readers only. Each state also has its own glyph (ring, disc, diamond, tick, hollow disc, square), so it reads without colour, and the glyph turns CanvasText in forced colours. Pulses stop under reduced motion. live makes one chip a polite status, so a change to Waiting for you is read out. As a button it reads the state, then actionLabel, and shows actionLabel as a tooltip.

components.name: SessionTimeline

It takes the agent_session.* events of core as they are (started, activity, finished) and sorts them by time; labels.activities names each activity slug and activityStates picks its state. An open session shows a running clock on its last event.

examples.code: <SessionTimeline events={events} labels={labels} />

components.a11y: An ordered list named by labels.list, so a screen reader announces the number of events and the position of each. Each event is a SessionStateChip, a word with its own glyph, never colour alone, and a time element with the machine-readable moment, formatted in the locale of the person. The duration and the running clock are timers with their label. Nothing in it takes focus.

components.name: SettingRow

components.name: SeverityBadge

components.name: ShortcutOverlay
components.description: A dialog that lists the keyboard shortcuts of an app in groups, opened with the ? key. CommandPalette can offer it through shortcutOverlay.

examples.code:

components.a11y: A modal dialog named by its heading: focus stays inside while open and returns to the trigger on close, and Escape closes it. The ? key opens it only when focus is not in a text field or an editable area. Each group is a labelled region with a list of terms, and every key is a kbd element, so a screen reader reads the action first and then its keys. On narrow screens it becomes a full-screen sheet.

components.name: Sidebar
components.description: The dark navigation column of the web apps: a flat list of links under plain headings, with the brand on top and the person signed in at the foot.   footer={<SidebarUser name="Ada Lovelace" description="Admin" signOut={{ label: 'Sign out', onPress: signOut }} />}>

components.name: SidebarNav
components.description: The flat list of links in a compact Sidebar. Give it the current route and it marks the matching link. Groups in it are plain headings; for nested navigation use SidebarRail.

  <NavItem href="/" icon={<Icon name="nav.home" />}>Dashboard</NavItem>

components.name: SidebarRail
components.description: The sidebar of the admin panels: a compact 72 px rail with one button per section. A section opens its panel to the side, a page with children opens another level further to the side, lined up with its row, and a third level the same way; nothing ever expands downward. Pick it for a panel with many sections, such as content, commerce, marketing and settings.

    { id: 'commerce', label: 'Commerce', icon: <Icon name="content.product" />, count: 12, countLabel: '12 orders to ship',
      groups: [{ label: 'Catalog', links: [
        { href: '/products', label: 'Products', icon: <Icon name="content.product" />,
          children: [{ href: '/products/variants', label: 'Variants' }, { href: '/products/brands', label: 'Brands' }] }
      ] }] }
  ]}
  current={pathname}
  labels={{ rail: 'Sections', pin: 'Keep the panel open', filterLabel: (s) => `Filter ${s}`, noMatches: 'No page matches.',
    currentSection: 'holds the open page', back: 'All sections', backTo: (label) => `Back to ${label}`, close: 'Close navigation' }}
  top={<SiteSwitcher />}
  bottom={<><ThemeMenu /><UserMenu /></>}
/>

<SidebarRail desktop="mac" sections={sections} current={pathname} labels={labels} />
// main process: new BrowserWindow({ titleBarStyle: 'hiddenInset' })

<SidebarRail sections={sections} current={pathname}
  labels={{ …, back: 'All sections', backTo: (label) => `Back to ${label}` }} />

<SidebarRail sections={sections} current={pathname} labels={labels}
  top={<SiteSwitcher />} bottom={<UserMenu />} />

components.a11y:
The rail is a named navigation of buttons: the up and down arrows, Home and End move between them, and each section button reports aria-expanded and controls the panel. Enter, Space or the right arrow opens the panel and moves focus into it; on a row with a chevron they open the next level to the side and move focus to its first link. The left arrow or Escape closes one level and returns focus to the row or button that opened it. Arrows, Home and End move inside one level. Each rail button is a Tab stop. The open page has aria-current="page", a filled pill and a heavier label, never colour alone; every row on the way to it and its rail button take the accent tone, and the current section is said in words. A mouse opens a level after a 150 ms hover, and a safe triangle keeps the level open while the pointer crosses the rows on its way to it. A floating panel closes on a click outside, Escape or a choice. Targets are at least 44 px. Below 48rem the menu button opens one modal drawer whose levels are screens that slide in, each with a back row such as "Back to Commerce". Motion lasts 180 ms and stops under reduced motion.

The strip is aria-hidden and holds no control, so nothing is lost to the drag region; the keys, names and targets are those of the web rail.

The menu button opens a modal drawer: focus moves in, stays in, and returns to the menu button on Escape. Only the top screen can be reached; the ones under it are inert. A new screen slides in over 180 ms, or appears at once under reduced motion. A row with a chevron opens the next screen. The back row is named by backTo, such as "Back to Commerce". The drawer opens on the screen of the open page.

Point at Commerce, then Products: each level opens to the side and never below. Enter, Space or the right arrow opens a level and moves focus in; the left arrow or Escape closes it and returns focus. Each rail button is a Tab stop. The open page and every row on the way to it take the accent tone, and only the page has aria-current="page". Below 48rem every level is a screen of the drawer with a back row.

components.name: SkipLink
components.description: SkipLink lets keyboard users jump past repeated navigation to the content. VisuallyHidden keeps text for screen readers only, such as the unit after a number or the name of an icon.

components.a11y: The skip link is hidden until it has focus, then appears in the top corner with a 44px target. Following it moves focus to the target as well as the scroll position, so the next Tab continues from the content. Prefer a visible label to hidden text wherever there is room.

components.name: SortHeader
components.description: The label and direction arrow of a sortable column. DataTable and Table use it already; use it alone for a custom header, with onSort when it should be a button.

examples.code:

components.name: Sparkline
components.description: A tiny trend with no axes, for a tile, a table cell or a line of text. Pick it when the shape matters more than the numbers.

examples.code: <Sparkline values={last28} label="Visits, last 28 days: rising from 1,204 to 1,530" />

components.a11y: One image with one name: the label has to say what the shape shows, in words. With fewer than two values it draws a dashed rule, and the label should say there is no trend yet. The line uses a system colour in forced colours.

components.name: Spinner
components.description: A small ring for a wait of unknown length, such as loading a list. Pick ProgressBar when the share of work done is known.

examples.code: <Spinner label="Loading projects" showLabel />

components.a11y: An indeterminate progress bar named by label. showLabel shows the same text without reading it twice. decorative hides it inside a control that already says it is busy. Under reduced motion it turns slowly instead of stopping, so it still says that work goes on.

components.name: SplitPane
components.description: Two panes with one divider, such as a form beside its live preview. The divider snaps to the given points while it is dragged, and storageKey keeps the width per screen. Use SplitView for three or more panes.

examples.code:

  endLabel="Preview"

components.a11y: The divider is a focusable separator named by label, with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax in percent of the first pane (valueText adds words), and aria-controls pointing at that pane. Arrow keys move it by step and follow the reading direction, Page Up and Page Down jump between snap points, Home and End go to the limits, Enter collapses and restores, a double click resets. On a touch screen its target is 44 pixels wide. startLabel and endLabel make the panes named regions.

components.name: Splitter
components.description: Panes divided by splitters that the pointer and the keyboard can move. Side by side panes stack below 40rem, so neither gets too narrow to read.

examples.code:

  <Pane>…</Pane>

  <Pane>…</Pane>

components.a11y: Each Splitter is a focusable separator that reports the share of the pane before it in percent and points at it with aria-controls. Arrow keys move it by 1%, Page Up and Page Down by 10%, Home and End to the limits, Enter collapses and restores; double click restores the starting split. Arrow keys follow the reading direction. When the panes stack on a narrow screen and scroll together, that column becomes a tab stop, named by label, so the keyboard can scroll it.

components.name: StackedBars
components.description: The parts of a whole for each row, such as page loads rated good, needs work and poor. Pick share to compare the mix between rows, and value to compare the totals as well.

components.name: StatCard
components.description: One number with its label, for the row of figures at the top of a dashboard. Give it href or onPress when the number leads to the full list.

components.a11y: The label is read before the value. With href or onPress the label becomes the link and the whole card is the target; the value is read as its description, and the focus ring surrounds the card. The icon is hidden and its tone colours only its tile. loading marks the card busy and reads loadingLabel; error shows a glyph and text in place of the value.

components.name: SubagentStat
components.description: Small read-only figures for a session: time, context used and subagents. Pick ToolbarStat for any other figure; the three others format their value and switch tone on their own.

examples.code:

<ContextStat label={t('context')} tokens={48210} window={200000} />

components.name: SwipeRow
components.description: A collection of cards that becomes one swipe row on phones, with previous and next buttons, a position counter and a hint, and a plain grid from the md breakpoint up. Use it for cards that would otherwise stack into a long column.

examples.code:
<SwipeRow
  label="Plans"
  previousLabel="Previous plan"
  nextLabel="Next plan"
  hint="Swipe for more"

components.a11y: On phones the row is a focusable region named by label: Arrow Left and Right move one card, Home and End go to the ends. components.name: Switch
components.description: An on and off setting that takes effect at once, with no save button. For a choice saved with a form, use Checkbox.

examples.code: <Switch defaultSelected onChange={setOn}>Sound on finish</Switch>

components.a11y: It is announced as a switch with its on or off state. The knob moves and shows a tick when on, so the state is a position and a glyph. Forced colours keep the knob in system colours.

components.name: Table
components.description: A read-only table on native table markup with a caption, row headers and optional sorting. Pick it for reports and summaries; on a phone it either scrolls in its own box or stacks each row into a labelled card.

examples.code:
<Table
  caption="Team members"
  columns={[
    { id: 'name', header: 'Name', isRowHeader: true, allowsSorting: true, cell: (m) => m.name },
    { id: 'seats', header: 'Seats', kind: 'numeric', cell: (m) => m.seats }

  rows={members}
  rowKey={(m) => m.id}
  layout="stack"
  sort={sort}
  onSortChange={setSort}
  emptyState="Nobody has joined yet."
/>

components.a11y: Native table semantics: the caption names it, sortable headers carry aria-sort and hold a real button, and row headers are read while moving down a column. The stacked layout keeps explicit table roles and shows each column name next to its value. A box that overflows becomes a focusable, named region so it scrolls from the keyboard. Loading is a polite status with aria-busy on the table; an error is an assertive alert.

components.name: TabPanel
components.description: Switches between panels of one view without leaving the page. Pick it when the panels belong together; use LinkTabs when each tab is its own address.

</Tabs>

Screen readers hear tab, position and selected state, and the panel is labelled by its tab. The underline is painted in Highlight under forced colours. The strip scrolls on its own when tabs do not fit, and vertical tabs stack above the panel on narrow screens.

components.name: TaskCard
components.description: A task from any connected tracker, as in the task list of the Agent. Pick it for lists where one task opens next to the list, and put the start button in actions.

examples.code:

components.a11y: The title is the card’s button or link and its hit area covers the card; actions sit above it and stay separately reachable. isCurrent sets aria-current with an accent rule. isPending sets aria-busy and shows a spinner with pendingLabel, and the card cannot be opened twice. components.name: TerminalBar
components.description: The strip under a terminal pane with tools that type into the session and figures about it. Pick it for any live agent session; turn it off while the agent waits for an answer.

examples.code:

  <ToolbarButton label={t('attach')} icon={<Icon name="action.attach" />} />
</TerminalBar>

components.a11y: A React Aria toolbar: one tab stop, arrow keys move between its controls and Tab leaves. While isDisabled is set every button is off and disabledReason says why in words next to them. The figures wrap onto their own line on a narrow pane.

components.name: TerminalScreen
components.description: A still picture of a terminal, such as the last lines of an agent session on an overview card. Pick it to preview; a live terminal needs xterm in the app.

examples.code: <TerminalScreen label="Claude Code session" title="claude · skriblyUI" text={lines} rows={12} showCursor />

components.a11y: The screen is a named group in the tab order and scrolls sideways inside its box. ANSI colour codes are removed, so screen readers get plain text. The cursor is decorative, hidden from screen readers, and only blinks without reduced motion.

components.name: Textarea
components.description: Multi-line text, such as a description or a note. Turn on monospace for Markdown or code, and add a counter when there is a limit.

examples.code:
<Textarea label="Description" maxLength={280}
  formatCount={(count, max) => `${count} / ${max}`} />

components.a11y: The counter sits in the description, so it is read when the field gets focus rather than on every key. Resize stays vertical so the page never scrolls sideways.

components.name: TextField
components.description: A labelled single-line field: names, titles, emails, URLs. It shows the four message tones: help in muted text, ok, info and warn with an icon, and the error.

examples.code:
<TextField label="Email" type="email" isRequired
  errorMessage="Enter an email address like name@example.com" />

components.a11y: The label, description, status and error are linked by React Aria; an invalid field sets aria-invalid and lists the error first. With isRequired and native validation the browser message shows on submit. Long words in messages wrap instead of overflowing.

components.name: ThemeProvider
components.description: Holds the theme mode, stores the choice and sets data-theme on the page. Put one at the root of an app; useTheme reads and changes the mode from any component below it. scoped themes a single panel, as here.

examples.code:

</ThemeProvider>

  const { mode, resolvedTheme, setMode } = useTheme()
  return <button onClick={() => setMode('dark')}>{resolvedTheme}</button>
}

components.a11y: Same as system follows the device, including a request for more contrast. The theme change animates from the pressed button only when motion is allowed. Contrast of every text and control pairing is tested in all three themes.

components.name: ThemeScript
components.description: An inline script for the head that applies the stored theme and reader settings before the first paint, so a dark page never flashes light. themeScript() gives the same source as a string for heads that React does not render.

examples.code:

</head>

<script is:inline set:html={themeScript()} />

components.a11y: Prevents a flash of the wrong theme and a jump in text size, both of which disturb readers with light sensitivity or low vision. Accepts a nonce for a strict Content Security Policy.

components.name: ThemeSwatch
components.description: An editor theme drawn as a little editor in its colours, with its name. With onPress it is a toggle for a grid of themes; without it a static preview.

examples.code:

  onPress={() => pick(theme)} isSelected={theme.id === active} selectedLabel={t('themes.selected')} />

components.a11y: A toggle button named by its visible text, the theme name first, pressed when chosen; the choice also shows as an accent border, a ring, a check and a word, and a thick system border in forced colours. The sketch is hidden from screen readers and keeps its colours in forced colours, as it is a picture of the theme. It lifts on hover only when motion is allowed.

components.name: ThemeToggle
components.description: Lets the reader pick light, dark, high contrast or the system setting. Use the segmented form in settings and the menu form in a crowded top bar.

examples.code:
<ThemeToggle
  label="Theme"
  options={{ light: 'Light', dark: 'Dark', contrast: 'High contrast', system: 'Same as system' }}
/>
<ThemeToggle variant="menu" label="Theme" options={options} descriptions={hints} />

The selected option shows a raised tile or a check mark, never colour alone, and stays visible in Windows high contrast. In a narrow container the words hide visually but stay in the accessible name.

components.name: Timeline

components.name: Titlebar

components.name: ToastProvider

components.name: ToggleButton

components.name: ToggleRow

examples.code: <ToggleRow title="Underline links" description="Links stand out by more than colour." />

components.a11y: The title and the switch are one wide target. The switch is named by the title and described by the text below it, and announces on or off.

components.name: ToneDot

components.name: ToolbarButton

components.name: ToolbarMenu

examples.code:
<ToolbarMenu label={t('changeModel')} icon={<Icon name="ops.cpu" />} value={model.label} title={t('model')}>
  {(close) => <RadioGroup label={t('model')} value={model.id} onChange={(id) => (pick(id), close())}>…</RadioGroup>}
</ToolbarMenu>

components.a11y: A non-modal dialog from React Aria: the trigger reports it is expanded, focus moves into the panel, Escape or a click outside closes it and focus returns to the trigger. The panel is named by its title or by label. On screens under 640px it becomes a sheet along the bottom edge that scrolls inside.

<SessionClock label={t('time')} since={session.startedAt} />
<ContextStat label={t('context')} tokens={48210} window={200000} />
<SubagentStat label={t('subagents')} count={3} running={1} runningLabel={(n) => t('running', { n })} />
<ToolbarStat label={t('toolCalls')} value="14" icon={<Wrench />} />

components.a11y: Each figure reads its label before the value, such as "Context: 48K · 24%". The clock is a timer, which screen readers do not announce on every tick. Near the limit ContextStat switches to a warning icon as well as a warning tint, and the percentage says the same; SubagentStat says how many run in words. Figures are text and take no focus.

components.name: ToolLine
components.description: One step an agent took between messages, such as reading a file or running a command. Add detail to let people open the output.

examples.code:
<ToolLine status={{ tone: 'danger', label: 'Failed' }} detail={<OutputBox label="Output" text={log} />}>
  Run npm test
</ToolLine>

components.a11y: The status word comes before the step, with an icon and a coloured edge, so it never rests on colour. With detail the line is a disclosure button with aria-expanded, opened with Enter or Space.

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: A short hint on hover or keyboard focus. Use it for extra words about a control that already has a name; for anything a touch user needs, use InfoTip.

examples.code:
<Tooltip content="Saves a copy you can return to later">
  <Button>Save version</Button>
</Tooltip>

components.a11y: Shows at once on keyboard focus and after a short delay on hover, stays while the pointer is over it, and Escape hides it. Its text describes the trigger through aria-describedby. IconButton has its own tooltip, so do not wrap it.

components.name: Topbar
components.description: The bar above the main column with search and icon actions. TopbarIcon is an icon button with a tip; give it isSelected for a toggle such as dark mode, or wrap it in a MenuTrigger.

examples.code:
<Topbar menuLabel="Open navigation">
  <SearchField … />
  <TopbarIcon label="Notifications, 3 new" badge="3"><Icon name="nav.notifications" /></TopbarIcon>
  <TopbarIcon label="Dark mode" isSelected={dark} onChange={setDark}><Icon name="theme.dark" /></TopbarIcon>
</Topbar>

components.a11y: The top bar is the banner landmark and wraps rather than clipping at 320px. TopbarIcon is named by its label, shows it as a tip on hover and keyboard focus, and a toggle reports aria-pressed. The badge is hidden from screen readers, so the label carries the count.

components.name: Tour
components.description: A guided walk that dims the page, rings one element per step and explains it in a bubble beside it. Use it once after sign-up or from a Help menu; steps whose element is missing are skipped and not counted.

examples.code:
<Tour isOpen={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}
  stepLabel={(n, total) => `Step ${n} of ${total}`}
  nextLabel="Next" backLabel="Back" finishLabel="Done" closeLabel="Close the guide">
  <TourStep title="A quick look around">Four stops, about a minute.</TourStep>
  <TourStep target="search" title="Search everything">Finds views and actions.</TourStep>
</Tour>
<IconButton data-tour="search" label="Search">…</IconButton>

components.a11y: The bubble is a modal dialog named by the step title and described by its text: the page behind is inert for screen readers and the pointer, and Tab stays in the bubble. Focus moves to Next on every step. Arrow keys step, Escape closes and focus goes back to what opened it. Each step is announced in a polite live region. On screens under 640px the bubble docks at the bottom; motion stops under reduced motion.

components.name: TourSpotlight
components.description: The dim and the ring a Tour draws, on its own, to point at one element, such as a new feature. It never blocks the pointer, so the page stays usable.

examples.code: <TourSpotlight target={element} showCursor />

components.a11y: Decoration only: hidden from screen readers, so say in words what it points at. The ring is a real border, which stays in forced-colors mode where the dim shadow is dropped. It moves without animation under reduced motion.
