components.name: TrackerBadge
components.description: The issue tracker an account or a task comes from, in settings and task lists.

examples.code: <TrackerBadge kind="jira" label="Jira" />

components.a11y: Decoration unless label is set. The letters name the tracker; red and green are kept for danger and success, so trackers whose own colour is one of them are neutral here.

components.name: TranslationStatus
components.description: The translation state of one entry per language: missing, draft, outdated when the source changed after the translation, and done. Pick it for an editor header or a list cell; with onSelect a chip opens that translation, and compact keeps only the language and the glyph in sight.

examples.code:
<TranslationStatus label={t('translations.label')} displayLocale={panelLocale}
  entries={[{ locale: 'de', state: 'outdated' }, { locale: 'uk', state: 'missing' }]}
  stateLabels={{ missing: t('missing'), draft: t('draft'), outdated: t('outdated'), done: t('done') }}
  onSelect={openTranslation} summary={(counts, total) => t('translations.done', { done: counts.done, total })} />

components.a11y: The chips are a named list. Each says its state with a glyph and a word, never colour alone; compact keeps the word for screen readers, and chips keep their edges in Windows high contrast. With onSelect each chip is a button named by the language and its state, such as "German: Outdated".

components.name: TreeRow
components.description: A hierarchy such as files or nested sections, with a folder icon that opens, badges and row actions. Pick it when depth matters; use List for flat records.

examples.code:
<TreeView aria-label="Files" selectionMode="single">
  <TreeRow id="src" title="src" icon={<Icon name="folder.closed" aria-hidden="true" />} expandedIcon={<Icon name="folder.open" aria-hidden="true" />}>
    <TreeRow id="index" title="index.ts" meta={<Badge tone="warn">Modified</Badge>} />
  </TreeRow>
</TreeView>

components.a11y: A treegrid with aria-level and aria-expanded on every row. Up and Down move, Right opens a branch or moves into it, Left closes it or returns to the parent, typing jumps to a row, and Enter or Space selects. The chevron has a localised Expand or Collapse name from React Aria and points the other way in right-to-left text. Indentation stops growing after eight levels so deep trees fit a phone.

components.name: UploadDropzone
components.description: Where files are added: a picker button, a drop area and the list of running uploads with progress and status. Use it on library pages; FileInput in forms keeps files with the form instead.

examples.code:
<UploadDropzone title="Upload files" buttonLabel="Choose files" dropLabel="or drop files here"
  description="JPEG, PNG or PDF, up to 20 MB each" acceptedFileTypes={['image/*', '.pdf']}
  maxFileSize={20_000_000} rejectedMessage={(files) => `Left out: ${names(files)}`}
  onFiles={upload} uploads={uploads} statusLabels={statusLabels}
  onRetry={retry} retryLabel={(item) => `Retry ${item.name}`} />

components.a11y: The drop area is a React Aria drop zone: keyboard and screen reader users can drop into it and paste a copied file while it has focus. The picker button is described by the accepted types. Each upload is a named progress bar with its status in words and a glyph. A finished upload is announced politely and a failed one at once, with its reason; progress itself is not announced, so it never talks over the page. Rejected files are listed in a warning that stays, and nothing leaves the list on its own.

components.name: VcsBadge
components.description: The git host of an account or a repository: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea or Azure DevOps. Pass the account avatar as src to show the person instead.

examples.code:
<VcsBadge kind="gitlab" label="GitLab" />
<VcsBadge kind="github" src={account.avatarUrl} size={36} />

components.a11y: Decoration unless label is set; leave it out when the host name is written next to it. The letters name the host, so the token colour is a hint only.

components.name: VirtualList
components.description: A List that renders only what is on screen, for thousands of results such as a file search. Give it a height; items are measured, so wrapped text and the compact density still fit.

examples.code:
<VirtualList aria-label="Files" items={files} className="h-72">
  {(file) => <ListItem id={file.id} title={file.name} meta={file.size} truncate />}
</VirtualList>

components.a11y: Behaves like List: arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down reach items that are not rendered yet, and the grid reports the full count with aria-rowcount and each item its position.

components.name: VisuallyHidden
components.description: SkipLink lets keyboard users jump past repeated navigation to the content. VisuallyHidden keeps text for screen readers only, such as the unit after a number or the name of an icon.

examples.code:
Skip to content
…
/file per file

components.a11y: The skip link is hidden until it has focus, then appears in the top corner with a 44px target. Following it moves focus to the target as well as the scroll position, so the next Tab continues from the content. Prefer a visible label to hidden text wherever there is room.

components.name: Wordmark
components.description: The written name with its first letter in the amber tile, for the front of a site or a splash screen. Use AppLockup in app chrome.

examples.code:
<Wordmark as="h1" size="xl" />
<Wordmark size="sm" tone="nav" />

components.a11y: The name is read once from a hidden copy and the drawn letters are hidden, so a screen reader never spells it in two parts. The xl size scales with the viewport and stops growing at 9rem. The tile gets a border in Windows high contrast.

components.name: WorkspaceRow
components.description: The sidebar of an agents view: each project, its main copy and worktrees, and the sessions in each, with the most urgent state rolled up. Pick it when sessions are grouped by where they run.

examples.code:
<WorkspaceTree label={t('workspaces')} selectedKey={open} onSelect={setOpen}>
  <WorkspaceRow id="notes" kind="project" label="notes" state={rollUpSessionState(states)} stateLabel={…}>
    <WorkspaceRow id="main" kind="workspace" label={t('mainCopy')} count={2} countLabel={t('sessions', { n: 2 })}>
      <WorkspaceRow id="s1" kind="session" label="@reviewer" state="blocked" stateLabel={t('state.blocked')} />
    </WorkspaceRow>
  </WorkspaceRow>
</WorkspaceTree>

components.a11y: A React Aria tree: arrow keys move, Right opens a branch and Left closes it, typing jumps to a row, and Enter or Space opens the row, which then reads as selected. Rolled-up states show their glyph and keep the word for screen readers; counts have their own words. Row buttons appear on hover, on keyboard focus and on the selected row, and always on touch screens. Long names are cut on screen, read in full, and shown whole in a native tip.
